title: Director of People Operations
description:
About ALSO.

We’re ALSO, an electric mobility company originally conceived as a part of Rivian. We’re a passionate team of builders, dreamers, doers and innovators, focused on creating entirely new (not to mention, innovative and delightful) vertically integrated, small EVs designed to meet the global mobility challenges of today and tomorrow. Our mission is to inspire everyone to ride ALSO—replacing many local car, truck and SUV miles with ones on vehicles that are more affordable, more enjoyable and 10-50x more efficient.



We’re bringing on a Director of People Operations to be the operational engine of our People function, driving the full spectrum of people programs. Total rewards is your core strength and the capability that complements our existing People team, but this role goes well beyond comp and benefits. You’ll build and scale the processes, infrastructure, and programs that support a fast-moving, global business, and you’ll do it with direct access to business leaders. This is a lean, high-trust role: you’ll report to our VP of People, lead a small team, and operate with the autonomy that comes from being close to the decisions that matter. If you’re energized by building the machine, not just running it, this is your kind of role.



What You'll Do

Total Rewards - Your Core Strength

•     Evolve and steward ALSO's compensation philosophy — job architecture, salary bands, leveling frameworks, and equity programs that work across our US and global teams

•     Lead compensation cycles on a regular cadence: merit, bonus, and additional equity grants, in close partnership with Finance and the VP of People

•     Own benefits strategy end-to-end — plan design, broker and vendor relationships, open enrollment, and ongoing benchmarking to ensure we remain competitive as we grow into new markets

•     Partner with the People Partner and Talent Acquisition on compensation for new hires and promotions, maintaining consistency and fairness at every level



People Operations & People Infrastructure

•     Partner with our People Ops Manager to evolve our HRIS and broader People tech stack, building on the deep investment of these systems and experience on the team — data integrity, system integrations, and self-service tooling that makes life easier for employees and managers alike

•     Build and maintain scalable People Ops processes across the full employee lifecycle: onboarding, offboarding, leave administration, performance cycles, and internal mobility

•     Ensure compliance across federal, state, local, and international employment law requirements — with a particular focus on our growing global footprint

•     Keep our people infrastructure lean and smart; we're not building for headcount, we're building for impact



Employee Experience & Engagement

•     Partner with the People Partner to develop and run employee engagement programs, recognition initiatives, and feedback loops that reflect ALSO's culture and values

•     Use people data and surveys to surface insights that help leadership make better decisions about our team



Team Leadership & Strategic People Partnership

•     Serve as a trusted advisor to the VP of People and senior leadership on compensation, org design, and people operations

•     Translate complexity into clarity — whether that's communicating a new comp framework to the team or presenting a benefits recommendation to the exec team

•     Lead and develop a small, high-impact team: setting clear priorities, modeling operational excellence, and creating an environment where people do their best work

•     Be a player-coach: you set direction and you also do the work, and you're proud of both



What You’ll Bring

We're looking for someone with deep roots in total rewards and the breadth to hold everything else that comes with running People Ops at a global, pre-IPO company. You'll likely bring:



•     8–12 years of progressive People or People Ops experience, with at least 5–7 years focused specifically on compensation, benefits, or total rewards

•     Experience leading people and programs in a high-growth or startup environment — you know what it means to build, not just maintain

•     Deep knowledge of compensation design, equity programs (ISOs, RSUs), and benefits administration in a multi-state and/or international context

•     Comfort operating across multiple geographies and navigating the compliance complexity that comes with global teams

•     Strong analytical skills — you can build a comp model and you know how to use data to tell a story that lands with leadership

•     High emotional intelligence and discretion; people trust you with sensitive information at every level of the org

•     A builder's mindset: you're energized by creating structure where there isn't any, and you don't need a large team to do great work



Nice to Have

•     Experience in EV, or consumer product companies

•     Familiarity with pre-IPO equity compensation and the complexity that comes with it

•     Experience supporting global market entry and the people infrastructure it requires

•     CCP, SHRM-SCP, or CEBS certification


The salary for this position ranges from $180,000 - $230,000 per year, depending on experience, qualifications, and location.

 

This is an onsite position requiring attendance in the office 5 days per week. Once fully ramped and in alignment with their manager, employees may have the opportunity for limited flexibility, including the potential to work remotely up to two days per week, based on business and team needs.

 

Perks & Benefits

 - Robust health coverage — excellent health, dental and vision insurance covered up to 100% by ALSO with FSA & HSA options

 - One Medical membership and dedicated insurance advocates

 - Rich fertility and family building benefits with Progyny

 - Flexible time off

 - 401(k) match

Why ALSO.

We’re passionate about helping the world find a better way to get there—wherever it is you’re headed.

We’re located in the heart of Silicon Valley and have brought together a world-class team from some of the biggest brands in the technology, automotive, cycling, outdoor recreation and retail spaces. 

Together we’re working hands-on to imagine, design and build an entirely new solution to a global set of transportation challenges.

title: Sales Associate (Part-Time), Los Angeles
description:
About ALSO.

We’re ALSO, an electric mobility company originally conceived as a part of Rivian. We’re a passionate team of builders, dreamers, doers and innovators, focused on creating entirely new (not to mention, innovative and delightful) vertically integrated, small EVs designed to meet the global mobility challenges of today and tomorrow. Our mission is to inspire everyone to ride ALSO—replacing many local car, truck and SUV miles with ones on vehicles that are more affordable, more enjoyable and 10-50x more efficient.




ALSO is looking for a Part-Time Sales Associate to support the launch and growth of our brand in/around Los Angeles. This is a field-based, customer-facing role that works closely with and reports to the Market Manager to bring ALSO to life through mobile demos, retail experiences, and community activations. You’ll be on the front lines—introducing customers to our vehicles, delivering exceptional experiences, and helping build the foundation of ALSO’s presence in Los Angeles.

This role is ideal for someone who is energetic, people-oriented, and excited to be part of an early-stage brand with room to grow.

 

What You Will Do

Customer Experience & Sales Support

 - Deliver engaging, high-quality customer experiences in both mobile and fixed retail environments.

 - Educate customers on ALSO vehicles, features, and benefits, guiding them through demo rides and early purchase consideration.

 - Support local sales goals by converting interest into qualified leads and sales.

 - Share customer feedback and insights with the Market Manager to improve execution and experiences.

Mobile Demo & Event Support

 - Assist with the setup, execution, and breakdown of mobile demo experiences and local activation events, including driving the custom Rivian EV van to/from events.

 - Safely operate and maintain the local demo fleet, ensuring vehicles are clean, charged, and customer-ready.

 - Represent ALSO at community events, pop-ups, and partner activations.

Retail Store Operations (in applicable markets, over time)

 - Support daily retail hub operations, including opening and closing procedures, merchandising, and general upkeep.

 - Deliver best-in-class customer service and demonstrate active selling skills.

 - Help create a welcoming, on-brand environment that reflects ALSO’s premium and playful ethos.

Operational Support

 - Follow operational, safety, and compliance processes as directed by the Market Manager and/or Market Coordinator.
   
   
   

What You Will Bring

 - 1+ years of experience in retail, events, sales, hospitality, brand ambassador, or customer-facing roles.

 - A positive, proactive attitude and willingness to jump in wherever needed - you actively engage in your professional development.

 - Strong interpersonal and communication skills—you enjoy talking to people, telling a compelling story, and actively selling products and services.

 - Ability to work in a dynamic, field-based environment, including weekends and events - you have a flexible work style and enjoy variety in your work schedule.

 - Interest in cycling, electric vehicles and/or innovative consumer brands - your enthusiasm for our brand is infectious!

 - Ability to work collaboratively while also taking direction and feedback well - you are a charismatic and fun team player!

 - A strong connection to, knowledge of and comfort riding a bike in Los Angeles is a plus!

 - Qualify as an authorized driver, meaning you are at least 21 years of age, have a valid U.S. driver’s license with a minimum of three (3) years of licensed driving experience, and can successfully complete a background screening and motor vehicle review - because you’ll be driving our demo van and fleet of bikes to meet customers where they like to ride!
   
   
   

This position offers an hourly pay rate of $21.00 per hour and is eligible to participate in the sales incentive program in accordance with the terms of the applicable plan. This role is expected to work approximately 20–24 hours per week. As a part-time position working fewer than 30 hours per week, this role is not eligible for company-sponsored benefits.

Why ALSO.

We’re passionate about helping the world find a better way to get there—wherever it is you’re headed.

We’re located in the heart of Silicon Valley and have brought together a world-class team from some of the biggest brands in the technology, automotive, cycling, outdoor recreation and retail spaces. 

Together we’re working hands-on to imagine, design and build an entirely new solution to a global set of transportation challenges.

10+ years of progressive sales experience in medical device, healthcare, or a related commercial environment.
5+ years of sales leadership experience managing regional or multi-state teams.

Strong experience in hospital sales, contracting, account management, and IDN or health system engagement.
Deep understanding of aesthetics, reconstruction, plastic surgery, general surgery, or adjacent surgical implant markets strongly preferred.
Demonstrated ability to build, develop, and motivate teams to exceed expectations.
Strong executive presence with excellent communication, negotiation, presentation, and relationship-building skills.
Proven ability to influence cross-functionally and operate effectively in a matrixed organization.

Comprehensive expertise in category management, including market analysis, cost and financial assessment, ensuring strategic and informed procurement decisions. Fluency in negotiation and bidding, adept in overseeing complex projects with a focus on effective change management.
Strong capabilities in internal stakeholder management and influence, aligning procurement strategies with business needs and fostering collaborative supplier relationships.

title: Associate Director, HEOR Strategy, Specialty
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
The Associate Director, Health Economics & Outcomes Research (HEOR) Strategy, Specialty will serve as the strategic HEOR lead for assigned assets within the Hypothyroidism Therapeutic Area. The role will develop and advance integrated evidence strategies supporting launch readiness, value demonstration, market access, differentiation, and lifecycle management, partnering across the Integrated Brand Team and broader organization to inform asset and business decisions.
As an individual contributor, the Associate Director will provide strategic and scientific leadership while leveraging V&E Centers of Excellence (COEs) and research partners for technical execution. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong strategic judgment, cross-functional influence, and leadership potential to assume broader responsibilities over time.
Responsibilities
Develop and evolve the integrated HEOR evidence strategy and roadmap , translating business, clinical, patient, and access evidence gaps into prioritized research initiatives aligned with asset strategy, launch milestones, and stakeholder needs.
Provide strategic and scientific direction across evidence-generation initiatives, including real-world evidence (RWE), patient and healthcare professional research, patient-reported outcomes, burden-of-illness and comparative-effectiveness research, and economic modeling.
Partner with V&E Centers of Excellence (COEs) and research partners to ensure methodological rigor, strategic alignment, prioritization, and timely evidence delivery while providing strategic direction and oversight .
Represent HEOR as a trusted strategic partner on cross-functional asset and launch teams, connecting insights across Commercial Marketing, Market Access, MHI/Value & Evidence, Clinical Development, Regulatory, and other relevant functions to inform integrated asset decisions.
Integrate and translate clinical, economic, humanistic, societal, and patient-centered evidence into a cohesive value narrative with clear implications for scientific, access, and business decision-making.
Anticipate changes in the payer, reimbursement, HTA, policy, and value-assessment environment and communicate implications, opportunities, risks, and recommendations to senior leaders and cross-functional decision-making forums.
Demonstrate leadership through influence, curiosity, and an enterprise mindset , using sound judgment and creativity to connect perspectives, build alignment, make timely decisions, and deliver in a fast-paced, ambiguous, and evolving environment .
Advanced degree in health economics or a related discipline, with a minimum of 5 years of relevant experience for candidates with a Master’s degree or a minimum of 3 years of relevant experience for candidates with a PhD or other relevant doctoral degree (e.g., PharmD, MD).
Strong knowledge of HEOR methodologies , with experience in areas such as RWE and observational research, patient-reported outcomes, economic modeling, burden-of-illness, comparative effectiveness, patient and healthcare professional research, and/or evidence synthesis.
Demonstrated ability to translate asset, business, patient, and stakeholder needs into strategic evidence priorities and actionable research questions .

Ability to analyze and understand technical information

Knowledgeable on multiple technologies and systems that support CSOC and CSIRT services (e.g., SOAR, SIEM, IPS/IDS, EDR, etc.)

Experience conducting stakeholder interviews, impact assessments, readiness assessments, focus groups, or similar discovery activities.
Demonstrated ability to develop audience-centered communications, presentations, job aids, training materials, and other change deliverables.
Ability to use qualitative and quantitative data to identify adoption barriers and recommend actions.

The IAM Enablement Analyst exists to make Identity and Access Management (IAM) services easier to understand, navigate, and use. Through these activities, the analyst will help increase self-service, reduce friction, and create a more consistent customer experience across IAM offerings.

The AbbVie Business Technology Solutions (BTS) team shapes the digital transformation necessary for our treatments to positively impact patients' lives. In this role, you will help turn IAM capabilities into intuitive, customer-centered experiences by improving user journeys, expanding self-service, and contributing to the development of a unified IAM portal.
About Our Team
This position is part of AbbVie's Information Security & Risk Management (ISRM) team within Business Technology Solutions and reports to the Associate Director, Customer Enablement & Innovation. Gathering and documenting user needs through interviews, surveys, feedback channels, support trends, and direct observation of IAM experiences.

Coordinating usability testing, pilot activities, and feedback reviews, then documenting findings and recommending practical experience improvements.
Supporting customer education, demonstrations, office hours, and adoption activities for IAM services and new self-service capabilities.
Tracking adoption, portal usage, customer feedback, self-service effectiveness, and other defined experience measures, and preparing concise insights for team leaders and stakeholders.
Identifying recurring user issues and process gaps, recommending automation or self-service opportunities, and helping validate whether implemented changes improve the experience.
Ensuring portal content, user guidance, and enablement materials follow applicable accessibility, security, privacy, compliance, and documentation standards.
Maintaining organized work items, decisions, requirements, dependencies, risks, and status updates for assigned enablement and portal initiatives.
Contributing to a culture of customer focus, collaboration, experimentation, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree with relevant professional experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Experience in business analysis, user experience, product support, customer enablement, digital experience, process improvement, information security, or a related technology discipline.
Experience gathering requirements and translating user or business needs into clear documentation, user stories, process flows, or actionable work items.
Experience creating user-facing documentation, knowledge content, communications, training materials, or self-service guidance.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts in clear, customer-friendly language.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate across product, engineering, operations, support, security, and business teams.
Customer-centered mindset with an interest in simplifying complex processes and improving how people interact with technology.
Ability to use feedback and data to identify patterns, recommend improvements, and measure results.

Familiarity with IAM concepts such as Identity Governance and Administration, Role Based Access Control, MFA, SSO and Federation, Privileged Access Management, access certifications, or identity lifecycle management.
Experience contributing to a portal, intranet, knowledge base, digital product, or self-service experience.

This is our  MD Fill - Aseptic Gown -  B2 night shift:  6pm-6:30am Wednesday - Friday & every other Saturday
Performs functions associated with cGMP manufacturing operations within the biologics production facility, including working with engineers in set-up and calibration tasks, as well as performing rework and quality testing related to the production of parts, components and final materials. Uses sophisticated programs (such as LIMS, SAP, automated control systems, etc.) to collect and evaluate operating data, which can be used to conduct on-line adjustments to products, instruments or equipment. Determines and may assist in developing methods and procedures to control or modify the manufacturing process.
Responsibilities
Must have the ability to become aseptic gown certified.
Shipping finished materials.
Maintaining inventory levels.
Sampling of in process and raw materials.
Running glass washer / autoclave.
Buffer / media preparation.
Equipment preparation (CIP / SIP).
Cell culture (from vial thaw to production scale).
Column chromatography.
Tangential flow filtration
Wear an aseptic gown during an 8 hr shift. This gown covers the full body.
Willing to complete a lot cleaning sanitation during the work shift
Follow all clean room entry and exit procedures
Wear the required aseptic gowning and PPE correctly at all times
Perform hand hygiene and sanitization before entering the clean room
Maintain aseptic technique to prevent contamination of materials and products
Sanitize work surfaces, tools, and equipment on a frequent and consistent basis
Minimize movement, talking, and unnecessary activity in the clean room
Inspect gowning and PPE for proper fit and integrity before use
Report any contamination concerns, spills, or equipment issues immediately
Handle sterile materials only in approved areas and in a controlled manner
Follow all environmental monitoring and cleaning requirements
Dispose of waste and contaminated materials according to procedure
Complete all required documentation accurately and on time. Good hand writing will be a huge plus.

Independently develop state-of-the-art capillary electrophoresis and chromatographic methods to characterize biotherapeutic proteins and their associated variants and impurities.

Supervise a team of one or more scientists and be accountable for the effective performance of the team.
Develop/optimize, qualify/validate, and transfer fit-for-purpose QC release and stability methods. Provide technical support and oversight for QC testing occurring at internal and external GMP laboratories.
Plan, author, and review regulatory submission documents, responses to health authority queries, technical reports, lab data, and method qualification/validation protocols.
Engage and influence the broader scientific community through publications and poster and oral presentations at industry conferences.
Degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Analytical Chemistry, or a related field. PhD with 6+ years, MS with 12+ years, or BS with 14+ years of relevant industry experience.

Demonstrated expertise in analytical method development for biologics, with strong hands-on experience in capillary electrophoresis and HPLC.
Experience supporting biologics CMC development, QC method qualification/validation, and method transfer.
Proven ability to interpret complex data, solve technical problems, and propose innovative scientific solutions.
Experience contributing to regulatory submissions, including quality and characterization sections, and responding to health authority questions.
Strong leadership, communication, and collaboration skills, with experience mentoring and supervising scientists.
Track record of scientific publications and conference presentations preferred.

Deep understanding of biologics analytics, impurity profiling, and protein characterization.
Ability to work effectively across functions and influence scientific and technical decisions.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Commitment to scientific excellence, quality, and continuous improvement.

AbbVie Analytical Research & Development (Analytical R&D) is a global analytical scientific organization responsible for all CMC analytical activities related to the development of AbbVie's pharmaceutical products.  Our scope includes AbbVie's diverse pipeline of innovative small molecule medicines and spans from the selection of Discovery candidate molecules to Late Stage Clinical.  We are building a world-class team of scientists and leaders who will drive the advancement of industry-leading analytical capabilities and make meaningful contributions to advance AbbVie's pipeline of innovative medicines.  Careers in AbbVie Analytical R&D provide unique opportunities to work with global and cross-functional teams to drive exceptional science and innovative product development strategies.  We are looking for diverse candidates with strong scientific experience to join the AbbVie Analytical R&D team and can offer exciting and rewarding career opportunities for these candidates.
Position Description:
This Senior Scientist – Solid State Characterization position will be in a technical specialty group - Physical Analytical Chemistry (PAC) withing Analytical R&D.  The PAC group is a global team of experienced and innovative scientists which utilize a diverse set of physical analytical tools to advance CMC development programs by providing insights and driving the understanding of materials, processes, and products.  Additionally, the group contributes to development and justification of control strategies and authors relevant sections of regulatory submissions across all development phases.
We are looking for a subject matter expert in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of drug substances (DS) and drug products (DP), from early form discovery through regulatory filing. The role focuses on single crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), electron diffraction (3D ED/MicroED), Rietveld refinement, quantitative phase analysis (QPA), and phase-appropriate polymorph quantitation methods both in drug substance and drug products. The scientist will work closely with Molecular Profiling Drug Development, Process Chemistry, Formulation, Process Engineering, Analytical, Operations, Quality Assurance and CMC-Regulatory.
Key Responsibilities:
Support new product development with advanced methods development and validations, technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements.
Serve as technical SME in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of DS and DP; Responsible for PXRD method development for DS and DP, validation/technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements
Serve as the PXRD expert for supporting solid form screening, identification, crystallinity, and stability studies; perform indexing, Pawley/Le Bail fitting, Rietveld refinement, and structure determination from powder data.
Perform quantitative phase analysis: Quantify polymorphic and amorphous content in DS and DP using Rietveld, whole-pattern, and multivariate approaches, addressing low drug load, excipient interference, preferred orientation, and micro absorption.
Apply advanced diffraction such as VT/VH-XRPD, in situ, synchrotron, and PDF analysis to study phase transformations and poorly crystalline/amorphous materials.
Apply SCXRD and 3D ED/MicroED structure determination, including absolute configuration and crystal packing of APIs, salts, cocrystals, hydrates, and solvates; generate calculated powder patterns and CIF reports.
Conduct orthogonal solid-state characterization including X-ray diffraction, thermal analysis, moisture sorption, microscopy, spectroscopy as applicable for solid form, impurity and stability studies
Support solid form control strategies per ICH Q6A, author Module 3 sections and health authority responses, and ensure GMP and data integrity compliance.
Highly autonomous and productive in performing laboratory work, method development and troubleshoot; processing, interpreting, and visualizing data to facilitate project team decisions

Understand and adhere to corporate standards regarding code of conduct, safety, appropriate handling of materials, controlled drug and radioactive compounds, and GxP compliance, where applicable.
Qualifications:
Bachelors, Masters, or Ph.D. in Chemistry, Material Science, Physics, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related field typically with minimum 10 (BS), 8 (MS), or 0 – 2 (Ph.D.) years related industry experience.
Strong technical background in solid state characterization, excellent analytical problem-solving, communication, presentation, and cross-functional collaboration skills. Capable of independently developing and troubleshoot analytical methods.
Extensive hands-on PXRD experience, including indexing, Rietveld refinement, QPA, and polymorph and amorphous quantitation.
Track record of developing and validating PXRD methods for DS and DP in a GMP environment, with knowledge of ICH Q2(R2), Q6A, Q14, and USP .
Expertise in small molecule SCXRD structure solution and refinement, including disorder modeling and absolute structure; and knowledge of 3D ED/MicroED approaches.
Proficiency with tools such as Olex2, SHELX, CrysAlisPro, TOPAS, Diffrac Eva and DQuant, GSAS-II, HighScore, Mercury, and the CSD.
Hands-on experience with DSC, TGA, hot-stage and polarized light microscopy, DVS, and strong data analysis and interpretation skills.

Experience with AI/ML and data science for automation of phase identification and Rietveld/QPA workflows, chemometrics, and Python or R scripting is preferred.
Experience with biophysical characterization tools of nanoDSC, DLS, SEC-MALS, CD, AUC, nanoDSF in peptide, LNP and biologic materials, formulations and process characterization is preferred.

Purpose:
Oversees the direction, planning, execution, and interpretation of clinical trials or research activities of one or more clinical development programs. Participates in cross-functional teams to generate, deliver, and interpret high-quality clinical data supporting overall product scientific and business strategy.
Responsibilities:
Manages the design and implementation of one or more clinical development programs in support of an overall Product Development Plan, based on strong medical and scientific principles, knowledge of compliance and regulatory requirements, AbbVie’s customers, markets, business operations, and emerging issues. Oversees project-related education of investigators, study site personnel, and AbbVie study staff.
Has overall responsibility for oversight of clinical studies, monitoring overall study integrity, and review, interpretation, and communication of accumulating data pertaining to safety and efficacy of the molecule. Along with Clinical Operations, is responsible for oversight of study enrollment and overall timelines for key deliverables. Responsible for assessment and reporting of serious adverse events per corporate policy and regulations for those protocols on which assigned.
Responsible for design, analysis, interpretation, and reporting of scientific content of protocols, Investigator Brochures, Clinical Study Reports, regulatory submissions and responses, and other program documents.
May oversee the work of Medical Directors and/or Scientific Directors, and of Clinical Scientists working on the same or related programs.
Provides in-house clinical expertise for the molecule and disease, coordinating appropriate scientific and medical activities with internal stakeholders as they relate to ongoing clinical projects. title: Power & Hydrogen Program Manager, Power & Hydrogen Solutions, GESA
description:
An execution-focused project/program manager responsible for the hands-on coordination and completion of power capacity and hydrogen fuel cell projects across the Amazon fulfillment network. This is a delivery role with a strong bias for action: the PM owns the details, gets into the field, and drives projects from feasibility through commissioning and handover. Oversees multiple concurrent projects spanning temporary and permanent power deployment (utility upgrades, generator installations, switchgear deployments, and air permitting) as well as hydrogen fuel cell execution — including decommissioning of existing assets, launch of new hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cells per Amazon standards and processes, and conversions of existing sites. Sets deadlines, assigns responsibilities, and personally tracks and unblocks progress. Prepares reports for upper management regarding the status of all projects.
Requires a bachelor's degree and at least 4 years of project management experience in power infrastructure, electrical systems, hydrogen/fuel cell systems, or a related area. The ideal candidate is a hands-on, detail-oriented operator who thrives in ambiguity, dives deep into technical and schedule details, and acts with urgency rather than waiting for direction. Must be familiar with a variety of the field's concepts, practices, and procedures across both power and hydrogen domains. Relies on sound judgment to plan and accomplish goals, and is comfortable rolling up sleeves — walking the site, reading the drawings, chasing the long-lead order, and closing out the punch list. Leads and directs the work of contractors, vendors, and cross-functional teams. A wide degree of creativity and latitude is expected to solve complex energy infrastructure challenges across diverse site conditions and regulatory environments. Typically reports to a manager or head of a unit/department.
Key job responsibilities
Project Management & Bias for Action
- Own delivery end to end and act with urgency — move projects forward every day rather than waiting for direction or escalation
• Get into the details: read the drawings, interrogate the schedule, understand the single-line and the hydrogen P&ID, and verify the numbers personally
• Be hands-on and in the field — walk the site, attend installation and commissioning activities, and verify work directly rather than relying solely on status reports
• Build and maintain the plan of record: detailed schedules, critical-path analysis, dependencies, risks, and clear owners and dates
• Proactively identify blockers and drive them to closure; dive deep on root cause and remove obstacles for contractors and cross-functional teams
• Run a tight operating rhythm — stand-ups, weekly reviews, and crisp written updates that make status and risks unambiguous
• Make decisions with incomplete information, bias toward action, and course-correct quickly as new data emerges
Program Coordination & Oversight
• Responsible for the coordination and completion of multiple simultaneous power and hydrogen execution projects across U.S. sites
• Oversee all aspects of the execution program from feasibility through commissioning and handover
• Set deadlines, assign responsibilities, and monitor and summarize the progress of all projects
• Prepare reports for upper management regarding program status, including monthly flash updates and executive summaries
• Lead and direct the work of contractors, vendors, consultants, and cross-functional teams
• Perform a variety of tasks ranging from technical design review to stakeholder management to regulatory coordination
Amazon Standards, Specifications & Quality Assurance
• Follow and verify that Amazon standards, specifications, and processes are met across all power and hydrogen infrastructure installations
• Ensure electrical equipment, switchgear, generators, fuel cells, hydrogen storage/dispensing systems, and associated systems comply with Amazon technical standards and design requirements
• Conduct quality reviews at each project phase to validate adherence to Amazon specifications before progressing to the next milestone
• Verify vendor deliverables, shop drawings, and equipment submittals meet Amazon engineering standards
• Coordinate with Amazon internal engineering teams to resolve specification questions and obtain approvals
• Document and track any deviations from Amazon specifications, securing proper waivers or corrective actions (e.g., Supplier Corrective Action Reports / SCARs)
Power Capacity Execution
• Drive execution of temporary and permanent power deployment projects — utility upgrades, generator installations, switchgear deployments, and service upgrades
• Oversee deployment of temporary and permanent natural gas and diesel generator systems (1–5MW scale), including rental genset mobilization and conversion to permanent power
• Manage utility coordination including transformer upgrades, switchgear installations, and service upgrades with utility companies
• Own the end-to-end switchgear (SWGR) procurement process: specification development, vendor selection, purchase order issuance, and delivery tracking
• Track SWGR lead times (typically 10–26 weeks) across all sites and ensure orders are placed to meet project timelines; monitor factory acceptance testing (FAT) and coordinate site delivery logistics
• Review and validate electrical designs, single-line diagrams, load calculations, and power distribution configurations
• Ensure compliance with NEC, NFPA, and local electrical codes
Hydrogen Fuel Cell Execution
• Decommissioning: Plan and execute safe decommissioning of existing hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cell assets — isolation, purging/inerting, asset removal, site restoration, and disposition in accordance with Amazon standards and applicable safety codes
• Infrastructure & fuel cell launch: Lead the launch of new hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cells per Amazon standards and processes — hydrogen storage and dispensing systems, hydrogen pads, piping, fueling infrastructure, and fuel cell power modules, from design review through installation, commissioning, and startup
• Conversions: Manage conversions of existing sites to hydrogen fuel cell operation (or between configurations), coordinating the transition sequencing, infrastructure modifications, and cutover to minimize operational disruption
• Coordinate with hydrogen fuel cell vendors and OEMs (e.g., Plug Power and equivalents) on equipment specifications, delivery schedules, and field support
• Verify hydrogen systems meet Amazon specifications and applicable hydrogen safety and fire codes (e.g., NFPA 2, NFPA 55) throughout design, installation, and commissioning
• Oversee fuel cell capacity planning, dispenser configuration, and integration with site power and operations
Procurement & Long-Lead Equipment Management
• Own procurement for long-lead equipment across both domains — switchgear, generators, fuel cells, and hydrogen infrastructure components
• Specify, order, track lead times, verify specifications, and coordinate delivery for critical-path equipment
• Coordinate with manufacturers and vendors on custom configurations and delivery schedules
• Escalate equipment delivery risks immediately when lead times threaten project schedules
Permitting & Regulatory
• Own the permitting process for all sites — air permit applications for stationary generator installations and hydrogen-related permits and approvals
• Prepare and submit permit applications across multiple jurisdictions and regulatory environments; track application status, agency review timelines, and approval milestones for each site
• Navigate complex permitting scenarios including CEQA approvals, non-attainment areas, emission offset requirements, and hydrogen/fire code approvals
• Coordinate with environmental and fire/life-safety consultants to develop applications, emission calculations, and hazard analyses
• Maintain a permit tracking log with submission dates, agency contacts, expected approval dates, and required follow-ups
• Proactively identify permitting risks and develop contingency plans to avoid schedule impacts; ensure all required emission and safety data is obtained from generator and fuel cell vendors
Project Execution & Delivery
• Drive the end-to-end project lifecycle: feasibility, design, procurement, permitting, installation, commissioning, and handover
• Develop and maintain detailed project schedules, budgets, risk registers, and status reports
• Coordinate contractor mobilization, equipment procurement, and installation activities
• Identify and resolve critical-path blockers with urgency; escalate issues proactively
• Rely on extensive experience and judgment to plan and accomplish goals under compressed timelines
Stakeholder Management
• Serve as the primary point of contact and single-threaded owner across all project stakeholders, aligning internal and external parties and holding each accountable to deliverables and timelines
• Customer — Amazon Operations: partner with Amazon Operations (the internal customer) to understand site requirements, manage expectations, minimize operational disruption, and secure buy-in through launch and handover
• General Contractor (GC): direct and hold the GC accountable for construction scope, schedule, RFIs, submittals, and field execution
• Engineer of Record (EOR) & Architect of Record (AOR): coordinate design intent, drawing reviews, RFIs, and design changes; ensure the installed work conforms to the stamped design
• Electrical Contractor (EC): coordinate electrical installation, terminations, testing, and energization activities and sequencing
• Air permitting agencies & consultants: engage regulatory agencies and environmental consultants (e.g., Trinity) to secure and maintain air permits and keep applications on the critical path
• Utility engagement — gas pipeline: drive utility coordination for natural gas pipeline connections, metering, pressure requirements, service applications, and interconnection timelines
• Equipment vendors & OEMs: manage generator, switchgear, fuel cell, and hydrogen infrastructure vendors on specifications, lead times, and field support
• Coordinate with Property/Construction Managers (PCMs) and Construction Managers at each site
• Provide weekly status updates and monthly program reports to leadership
Site Launches, Commissioning & Energization
• Travel to project sites during critical installation, commissioning, and decommissioning phases
• Oversee equipment startup, testing, and acceptance procedures for both power and hydrogen systems
• Ensure safe energization, hydrogen system startup, and transition to operations

- 4+ years of defining and executing against program timeline & requirements experience
- 4+ years of driving end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership experience
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams
Preferred qualifications: - 4+ years of managing stakeholders in cross-functional project experience
- 4+ years of vendor management experience
- Experience in stakeholder management, dealing with multiple stakeholders at varied levels of the organization
- 4+ years of leading large complex programs experience

title: AI Applied Scientist, AI Evaluation Science
description:
AI systems are only as trustworthy as the methods used to evaluate them. At Apple, where AI powers experiences for billions of people, getting evaluation right is not a support function, it is a foundational science. Our team, part of Apple Services Engineering, is building that scientific foundation: rigorous, scalable evaluation methodology for LLMs, agentic systems, and human-AI interaction. Our goal is evidence that teams can act on: what to measure, whether a change helped, why a system failed, and whether it is ready to ship.
What makes this team unusual is its interdisciplinary core. You will work alongside measurement scientists (psychometrics, validity theory), ML researchers, and platform engineers, bringing together ML research, statistical rigor, and production engineering.
We are looking for an Applied Scientist who works across the full arc of evaluation science: turning research into tools engineers can use on their own, and turning what those engineers run into new research. You care whether a method holds up on real data, at real scale, for a real decision, and you are curious enough to go after the open question underneath when it doesn't.
Our team is building self-service evaluation: tools, SDKs, and AI-powered capabilities that let engineers across Apple evaluate their AI features on their own, quickly and correctly, so they can build and ship those features faster. You will develop the methods that make this possible: raising the quality of the evaluations engineers run, and helping them understand what their results mean and what to do next. Often the method a problem needs doesn't exist yet. When that happens, you will figure it out, whether that means extending a recent paper or developing something new, and share what you learn through publications and internal research reports. We are looking for individuals across a range of experience levels.
With research and measurement scientists, you will co-develop new methods, make sure the tools give engineers valid, trustworthy signals, and bring back the hard problems that should shape the team's research agenda. With platform and research engineers, you will define what each method needs to work reliably without an expert in the loop, including its assumptions, failure modes, and validation tests, so it can ship in the evaluation SDKs and APIs used across Apple.
The successful candidate combines scientific depth with practical judgment: you know which methods fit a problem and why, can design experiments that show whether they actually work, can diagnose why they break down on messy real-world data, and can explain clearly what an evaluation result does and does not support.
Minimum qualifications: Ph.D. in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, or a closely related field, or a Master's degree in one of these fields with 3+ years of applied research experience.
Deep expertise in evaluating AI systems, gained through research on evaluation methods, substantial hands-on experience evaluating LLMs or agentic systems in real products, or both.
Strong proficiency in Python and the modern ML ecosystem, with demonstrated ability to implement complex methods from recent papers and run large-scale experiments.
Hands-on experience with large language models, whether fine-tuning, inference, prompting pipelines, or building LLM-powered applications.
Demonstrated research ability through publications at peer-reviewed venues, preprints, or equivalent research output.
Track record of applying research to practical problems: methods, prototypes, or tools adopted by other teams or used to inform real product decisions.
Solid software engineering fundamentals for research code: version control, testing, reproducibility, and code others can build on.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex results, and their limitations, to diverse audiences.
Comfort with ambiguity and new problem spaces; you thrive when building something that doesn't yet have a playbook.
Preferred qualifications: First-author publications at top-tier venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP), especially on evaluation methodology: papers about how to evaluate, not just papers that use evaluation to demonstrate model improvements.
Specific experience in one or more of: LLM-as-judge approaches (calibration, rubric design, bias mitigation); benchmark design and validation (IRT, contamination detection); human evaluation methodology (protocol design, quality control); experimentation and comparisons between system versions (A/B testing, uncertainty quantification); or agentic and multi-agent system evaluation, including failure diagnosis and automated red-teaming.
Familiarity with theoretical foundations of evaluation: measurement theory and validity frameworks, statistical learning theory (calibration, reliability, decision theory), causal inference, or preference aggregation.
Experience with the practical challenges of evaluating generative AI and agentic systems: non-deterministic outputs, token economics, multi-turn agent trajectories, and tool use.
Experience building methods or tools used directly by non-experts, such as developer-facing ML tooling or self-service analytics.
Familiarity with modern evaluation tools and frameworks (e.g., DeepEval, Ragas, TruLens, LangSmith, or agent tracing and observability tools).
Experience working with distributed computing or cloud-native tooling (e.g., Ray, Spark, Docker/Kubernetes) to run evaluations at scale.
Experience with cross-disciplinary work, such as collaboration with social scientists, psychometricians, or domain experts.
Experience in fast-moving, early-stage teams where you helped define technical direction from the ground up.

What makes this team unusual is its interdisciplinary core. You will lead ML researchers, measurement scientists, and applied scientists, bringing together frontier ML research, psychometric and statistical rigor, and production engineering. title: Wireless System Design Engineer
description:
Imagine what you could do here. At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Bring passion and dedication to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish.
The people here at Apple don’t just build products — they craft the kind of wonder that’s revolutionized entire industries. It’s the diversity of those people and their ideas that inspires the innovation that runs through everything we do, from amazing technology to industry-leading environmental efforts. Join Apple, and help us leave the world better than we found it.
Our manufacturing wireless footprint grew 200% between 2024 and 2026, and we forecast
another 50% growth each year. Every new deployment adds clients, access points, and tighter
latency budgets to factory RF environments that are already crowded.
We are hiring a Wireless System Design Engineer to architect, secure, and debug these networks
at scale. You will own end-to-end wireless design on the factory floor:
• Spectrum and channel planning for dense deployments
• Low-latency design for time-critical test traffic
• Secure onboarding of thousands of device
When something breaks, you will lead root-cause analysis across client, AP, controller, and host
logs. You will also build the AI-driven analysis that makes this correlation fast, repeatable, and
increasingly automatic. You will partner with local operations, test, and network teams during new production line launches, so issues are resolved before they block production.
Minimum qualifications: 10+ years of experience in wireless and RF engineering, including hands-on design and
deployment on at least one enterprise Wi-Fi platform (e.g., HPE Aruba, Cisco
Catalyst/Meraki, Juniper Mist, Extreme, Ruckus).
Working knowledge of network access security and device identity: certificate-based
authentication, RADIUS, PKI, and zero-touch provisioning.
Wireless system design experience: spectrum and channel allocation in dense networks,
RF planning and site surveys, quality-of-service design, and low-latency tuning.
Solid networking fundamentals, including IP addressing and services, VLANs, and
routing.
Demonstrated use of AI to automate debugging, such as LLM- or ML-based workflows
that correlate logs, detect anomalies, or propose root causes, with results you can
describe and measure.
Python and Bash development skills: building and maintaining tools others rely on, with
version control, code review, and testing.
Preferred qualifications: Wireless deployments in manufacturing, industrial IoT, or other high-density, mission-
critical environments.
Familiarity with RF simulation and predictive planning tools, network security policy and
segmentation for device fleets, and Bluetooth or other short-range wireless coexistence
with Wi-Fi.
Industry certifications such as CWNE, CWNA, CWDP, CWAP, or vendor equivalents
(ACMX, CCNP Wireless)

title: Project Leader, Consumer and Retail
location: Durham, North Carolina, United States of America
description: Who We Are Boston Consulting Group partners with leaders in business and society to tackle their most important challenges and capture their greatest opportunities. BCG was the pioneer in business strategy when it was founded in 1963. Today, we help clients with total transformation-inspiring complex change, enabling organizations to grow, building competitive advantage, and driving bottom-line impact. To succeed, organizations must blend digital and human capabilities. Our diverse, global teams bring deep industry and functional expertise and a range of perspectives to spark change. BCG delivers solutions through leading-edge management consulting along with technology and design, corporate and digital ventures - and business purpose. We work in a uniquely collaborative model across the firm and throughout all levels of the client organization, generating results that allow our clients to thrive. Practice Area BCG's Consumer Practice creates breakthrough strategies for clients across all consumer sectors, including Consumer products, Fashion & Luxury, and Retail. Our aspiration: BCG as the most influential company in the global consumer industry. The consumer environment and consumer behaviors are fundamentally changing as innovation and ecosystems continue to evolve. We work collaboratively to create profound and competitive impact at marquee clients. Inventing the future with the most-industry shaping ideas and capabilities. What You'll Do As a member of our consulting team, you will manage the design and development of long-term business strategies for consumer and retail clients in the areas of go-to-market strategy, operating model design, organizational design, and value creation in order to optimize revenue growth and organizational capability. Specific duties include: perform sophisticated market research, benchmarking, market sizing, modeling, forecasting, and decision analysis to identify growth opportunities; design and lead supply chain and distribution strategies for consumer and retail clients, including network design, inventory deployment, 3PL sourcing, and transportation optimization to reduce cost-to-serve and improve service levels; analyze fulfillment and distribution performance using operational and financial metrics to identify performance gaps and improvement opportunities; develop KPI dashboards, reporting frameworks, and compliance remediation strategies, including chargeback prevention, dispute resolution, and documentation controls; design supply chain operating models, organizational structures, governance frameworks, and implementation roadmaps; and lead large-scale operations and digital supply chain transformations, including WMS and TMS enablement, automation initiatives, omnichannel fulfillment, and integration of demand planning with S&OP processes; manage case team responsibilities including personnel assignments, research and analysis, and reports to clients; undertake critical evaluation of analytical work performed using advanced economics and financial analysis techniques; oversee and direct consultants and junior professional staff, and oversee project planning and preparation of outputs; and present findings to senior client management, and oversee business development and client relationships. What You'll Bring The position requires a Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Economics, Management, or related field (willing to accept foreign education equivalent) plus three (3) years of experience as a management consultant or business analyst which must include at least one (1) year of experience providing business strategy recommendations focusing on operational efficiency and revenue growth to companies in the consumer and retail sector. In lieu of Bachelor's degree and three (3) years of experience as noted above, BCG will accept a Master's degree (or foreign education equivalent) in Business Administration, Economics, Management, or related field and one (1) year of experience as a management consultant or business analyst which must include at least one (1) year of experience providing business strategy recommendations focusing on operational efficiency and revenue growth to companies in the consumer and retail sector. Specific skills/other requirements (quantitative experience requirement not applicable to this section) - must possess the following: analyzing operational and transactional data sets, including warehouse management system (WMS), enterprise resource planning (ERP), order, transportation, and customer deduction and claims data, leveraging Excel, SQL, Alteryx, Tableau, and Power BI to isolate drivers of operational failure and financial leakage; building cost-to-serve and total cost of ownership models for distribution and fulfillment networks, including activity-based cost allocation, labor standards and productivity modeling, freight and accessorial cost modeling, and scenario analysis of network, flow-path, and outsourcing alternatives; applying retail customer compliance and vendor requirement frameworks, including retailer routing guides, electronic data interchange (EDI) transaction sets such as advance ship notice (856) and invoice (810), packaging, labeling, and value-added services (VAS) standards, and retailer penalty and deduction schedules, to assess compliance exposure and design preventive controls; designing operational performance management systems, including KPI hierarchies and dashboards, service level agreement (SLA) definition, third-party logistics (3PL) provider scorecards and governance forums, and weekly and monthly performance review cadences; applying consumer and retail commercial frameworks, including consumer and channel segmentation, assortment and price-pack architecture, customer and account profitability analysis, and demand forecasting, to align supply chain and operations decisions with go-to-market and commercial strategy; applying advanced economic and financial analysis theories including competitive cost and decision analysis, capabilities assessment, portfolio review based on financial reports, and experience and scale curve analysis; conducting advanced analysis of scale economies, seasonal effects on financial forecasts, impact of uncertainties on business outcomes, corporate financing policies, and evaluation of factors that influence a company's debt capacity; and managing individuals, teams and processes. Additional info Multiple positions available. Applicants will only be considered for Durham, North Carolina office location. Partial telecommute benefit available. Must report to and reside within commutable distance of the listed BCG office. Domestic/international travel required (up to 80%) based on client/company need. M-F, 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. 45+ hours per week. Salary range: $225,400.00 - $252,900.00 per year. In addition to your base salary, you will also be eligible for an annual discretionary performance bonus and BCG's Profit Sharing and Retirement Fund (PSRF) contribution. BCG also provides a market leading benefits package described below. At BCG, we are committed to offering a comprehensive benefit program that includes everything our employees and their families need to be well and live life to the fullest. We pay the full cost of medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees - and their eligible family members. * That's zero dollars in premiums taken from employee paychecks. All our plans provide best in class coverage: Zero dollar ($0) health insurance premiums for BCG employees, spouses, and children. Low $10 (USD) copays for trips to the doctor, urgent care visits and prescriptions for generic drugs. Dental coverage, including up to $5,000 (USD) in orthodontia benefits. Vision insurance with coverage for both glasses and contact lenses annually. Reimbursement for gym memberships and other fitness activities. Fully vested retirement contributions made annually, whether you contribute or not. Generous paid time off including vacation, holidays, and annual office closure between Christmas and New Years. Paid Parental Leave and other family benefits such as elective egg freezing, surrogacy, and adoption reimbursement. Employees, spouses, and children are covered at no cost. title: Production Control Supervisor
description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

The Production Control Supervisor leads our hourly warehouse, receiving, and lineside delivery teams — managing material flow across a fast-paced manufacturing environment. You'll establish and drive operational KPIs while overseeing materials from receiving and storage through kitting, line-side delivery, and shipping.

This role demands high inventory accuracy, strong safety performance, and consistent support for production teams. You won't accept the status quo — you'll identify waste, drive continuous improvement, and communicate cross-functionally to remove blockers and keep production running without interruption.

 

What You'll Do

People Leadership

 - Supervise, coach, and develop an hourly workforce — including performance feedback, conflict resolution, corrective actions, and performance improvement plans.

 - Lead by example with a strong floor presence and clear expectations for safety, quality, and productivity.

 - Monitor staffing levels, timekeeping, attendance, and shift coverage.

Warehouse & Materials Operations

 - Oversee receiving, inspection handoff, material board review, put-away, storage, picking, kitting, line-side delivery, and shipping operations.

 - Ensure material availability to production at agreed service levels while minimizing excess inventory and handling.

 - Maintain accurate inventory through disciplined cycle counts, transaction execution, and audits.

 - Enforce FIFO, shelf-life controls, and material segregation requirements.

 - Supervise internal logistics, milk runs, and material replenishment routes.

Safety, Quality & Equipment

 - Ensure compliance with company procedures and quality standards.

 - Ensure proper operation, state of charge, and maintenance of material handling equipment (forklifts, pallet jacks, ladders).

Continuous Improvement & Cost Control

 - Identify and lead process improvements to increase throughput, accuracy, and labor efficiency.

 - Drive waste reduction across space, motion, handling, and inventory.

 - Analyze operational metrics and implement corrective actions where targets are not met.

Systems & Reporting

 - Ensure accurate and timely transactions in ERP/WMS systems.

 - Track and report KPIs including inventory accuracy, on-time delivery, productivity, safety, and quality.

 - Collaborate cross-functionally with manufacturing, quality, supply chain, engineering, and logistics teams.
   
    

What You'll Bring

 - Bachelor's degree or 5+ years of experience in warehouse, materials, manufacturing, or supply chain operations.

 - 1+ year of experience leading or supervising hourly teams in an operational environment.

 - Strong understanding of inventory control, material flow, and production support.

 - Experience with ERP/WMS systems (Odoo, SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, or similar).

 - Proficiency in Microsoft Office with advanced Excel skills.

 - Ability to operate material handling equipment including forklifts; able to lift up to 75 lbs and work at heights with or without accommodation.

 - Willingness to work extended hours, weekends, or alternate shifts as required.

 

About the Team

The Production Control team exists to ensure every part, kit, and shipment is exactly where it needs to be — at the right time, in the right quantity, and in the right condition — so production can move without interruption. Our work directly enables Base to build and deploy reliable energy systems by creating a materials operation that is accurate, disciplined, and built for scale. The challenges we solve are tangible and high-impact: preventing line stoppages, protecting inventory integrity, and designing material flow that can keep up with rapid growth.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

As the Director of Consumer Growth Analytics, you’ll use your quantitative background to lead other data scientists and dive into large datasets to guide decision-making. Experience leveraging AI coding tools to improve productivity and harden repeatable processes without sacrificing accuracy or code quality (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor)
The insight to take ambiguous problems and solve them in a structured, hypothesis-driven, data-supported way

location: Seattle, WA; Los Angeles, CA, Chicago, IL; Austin, TX; Denver, CO; Atlanta, GA; Miami, FL; Boston, MA; Washington D.C.
description:
About the Team
Audience Insights brings the voices of consumers, Dashers and merchants into decisions across DoorDash. Our work spans audiences, markets and business problems, giving researchers the opportunity to apply their skills in many different ways. We are expanding how we connect learning globally, combine survey and behavioral data, and use AI to find patterns in quantitative and qualitative research.
About the Role
In this remote US role, you will lead brand insights, helping the business set the right goals, track progress and improve creative before and after launch. You will lead 3 manager-level roles, including 1 opening, with Canada in the direct team and dotted-line consultation for Australia and other markets and brands. You will own work end to end while developing the team and shaping the next chapter of our brand-to-business learning. You will report into the Head of Audience Insights on our Audience Insights team in our Marketing organization.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Shape brand goals: Guide meaningful metrics and targets grounded in history, business context and the decisions partners need to make.
Own the brand foundation: Lead tracking across audiences and measurement levels, protect quality and comparability, and turn reporting and ad hoc analyses into actionable insight.
Improve creative: Lead pre- and post-testing and build focused diagnostics that guide campaign development and specific optimizations.
Connect the evidence: Combine survey, behavioral and qualitative learning, use AI thoughtfully, and identify new opportunities and future analytical questions in existing data.
Develop people and drive decisions: Coach managers, guide vendors and partners across markets, and deliver reports and presentations that shape marketing strategy and action.
We’re excited about you because…
You bring deep research experience: You have 8+ years in Market Research or Insights, with end-to-end ownership of studies that inform brand and marketing decisions.
You know brand tracking in depth: You have owned recurring programs across multiple levels, such as masterbrand and category, and use crosstabs, statistical testing and indexing to interpret metrics, investigate movement and protect sample, weighting and trend comparability.
You choose methods to fit the question: You understand concept development, script and copy testing, ethnography, segmentation, brand health and other qualitative and quantitative approaches, including when to use each and how to connect the learning.
You write surveys that work: You write questionnaires from scratch and understand how tools such as Qualtrics use display and skip logic, piping, randomization, quotas and response validation, so you can specify requirements, guide programming and test that the survey works as intended.
You own research end to end: You turn business questions into proposals and learning plans, explain methodological choices to non-researchers, and manage execution, vendors, analysis and reporting through to recommendations.
You turn understanding into action: You are curious about what makes people tick and translate complex evidence into compelling stories that shape brand strategy, improve campaigns and uncover growth opportunities.
You develop people and lead collaboratively: You coach researchers, set priorities and bring creativity to solving challenging problems with your team, vendors and business partners, building trust and influencing decisions across markets while staying close to research quality.
You apply AI with research judgment: You have used AI to strengthen analysis, synthesis or research workflows, can explain how you validated the output, and can help others use these tools effectively while owning the conclusions.
We expect this position to be filled by 01-16-2027

About the Team
Join us at DoorDash, where our people are our most valuable asset. As a member of our Architecture and Security team, you’ll play an instrumental role in building simple experiences with technology. We’re looking for a talented Solutions Architect, Business Technology Security to join our team and work closely with our business partners to drive key business decisions and innovate in critical tools such as Workday and the custom tools and dashboards we build on top of it.
About the Role
The DoorDash Architecture and Security team is looking for a Solutions Architect, Business Technology Security with demonstrated experience and knowledge in Workday Security. This role owns the strategy and design of Workday security architecture, and ensures it translates correctly into the custom, in-house tools and dashboards built downstream of it. This is a strategy and design-focused role so success here depends heavily on your ability to gather clear requirements, write them up well, and communicate design decisions to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. You will interact directly with senior leaders and cross-functional partners across DoorDash to capture requirements and design lasting, secure solutions that hold up across the full ecosystem.
This role will report to the Sr. Manager, Architecture and Security.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Own the strategy and design of Workday’s security architecture — data models, security groups, domains, and business process security — that serves as DoorDash’s security source of truth for the People organization.
Translate that architecture into clear requirements and design documentation that our build team can implement, and that downstream custom tools and dashboards can be built against safely.
Review new or proposed custom tooling and downstream reporting needs to identify security touchpoints and data access implications before they’re built, advising on the right design approach.
Partner with process owners to define data security policies, protocols, and procedures that protect sensitive HR data across Workday and downstream systems.
Conduct regular audits and risk assessments across Workday and the tools and reporting layers downstream of it, maintaining a forward-looking security and data classification roadmap.
Serve as the subject matter expert on security, data, and reporting capabilities and limitations, communicating trade-offs clearly to both build teams and non-technical business stakeholders.
We’re excited about you because…
You have 5-7 years of work experience in HRIS implementation and configuration, both domestic and international, with deep expertise in Workday Security.
You have extensive experience with one or more Workday HCM modules (Core HCM, Reporting, Payroll, Time & Labor, Compensation, Talent Management, Absence Management) and understand how their security models interact.
You are an excellent requirements writer — you can turn an ambiguous business or security need into a clear, detailed design or requirements document that another team can build from without having to guess your intent.
You have experience translating Workday security and data architecture into requirements for downstream, custom-built tools and reporting systems.
You have a BA/BS degree in a quantitative or business field, or equivalent work experience.
You have excellent written and verbal communication skills, comfortable presenting design recommendations to senior stakeholders and handing off clear specs to a separate engineering or build team.
We expect this position to be filled by 01/14
Compensation

Base salary is localized according to an employee’s work location. Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future.
In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants. Talk to your recruiter for more information.
DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others.
To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here .
