title: Product Manager - Chicago, IL
description:
About MISUMI Americas
MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.
Impact In This Role:
As a Product Manager at MISUMI Americas, you will own a defined product area — whether a feature set, a workflow, a capability, or a segment of our platform — and be responsible for delivering strong, well-executed product work within it. You will gather and synthesize customer, stakeholder, and performance insights; write clear requirements; partner closely with Engineering and Design on delivery; and track outcomes to drive continuous improvement.
This role is designed for someone who is serious about the craft of product management and is ready to build the depth of judgment and business understanding needed to take on broader ownership over time. You will be expected to deliver reliably, communicate clearly, build credibility with your cross-functional partners, and show increasing independence as you develop fluency in the domain. The best PMs in this role will grow into Senior PMs who own full product areas with strategic autonomy.
You will report to the VP, Product Management.
Areas of Responsibility:
Business acumen and domain awareness
Develop a deep understanding of the customers, internal users, and business context relevant to your product area — including how your work connects to broader platform goals and company priorities
Research and synthesize customer needs, stakeholder feedback, and operational realities to build a clear, grounded point of view on the problems your team should be solving
Assess the needs of internal users across Operations, Sales, and other functions, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and remove friction in workflows that touch your area
Stay current on how your product area is performing — tracking metrics, monitoring trends, and developing hypotheses about where the biggest opportunities for improvement lie
Build familiarity with the competitive landscape and with how MISUMI Americas' platform capabilities compare to alternatives available to our customers
Roadmap contribution, work analysis, and scoping
Contribute to roadmap development within your area with increasing independence, translating high-level goals into clearly scoped objectives, projects, and requirements
Develop and maintain a framework for tracking input and output metrics that provide a quantitative view of the success and impact of your work
Build business cases for prioritized initiatives, articulating the customer value, business rationale, and expected outcomes in a way that earns stakeholder confidence
Scope and define requirements for roadmap items with clarity and specificity — ensuring Engineering and Design have what they need to build the right thing, efficiently
Proactively identify trade-offs and risks associated with scope and sequencing decisions, and work collaboratively with your team to develop pragmatic mitigation approaches
Establish and communicate a well-reasoned point of view on the problems your team should prioritize and why
Cross-functional collaboration
Build strong working relationships with Engineering, Design, Operations, Sales, and other functions — earning trust through clear communication, good judgment, and consistent follow-through
Lead cross-functional meetings within your area to align on scope, priorities, and requirements — ensuring that all relevant perspectives are heard and decisions are made with shared understanding
Actively seek feedback from stakeholders and adjust plans accordingly, fostering a responsive and collaborative approach to product development
Work with cross-functional partners to develop and evaluate hypotheses about customer needs and solutions, bringing both rigor and creativity to discovery
Communicate team progress and results to stakeholders with transparency — celebrating wins and ensuring the organization learns from setbacks
Execution and risk management
Apply Agile methodologies to organize and manage sprints, supporting a streamlined and efficient development process within your team
Partner closely with Engineering to estimate scope and timelines, continuously refining plans as work progresses and new information emerges
Keep stakeholders informed of project status, proactively flagging risks or deviations from plan and proposing solutions rather than just surfacing problems
Drive product launches by ensuring that all relevant parts of the organization — Engineering, Operations, Sales, Marketing, and Support — are prepared and aligned
Analyze metrics post-launch to evaluate impact, identify gaps, and inform the next iteration of your roadmap
Travel up to 10% annually for team collaboration, customer research, and training
Desired Traits and Qualifications, Education and Experience Equivalency:
Past Experience:
2–4 years of product management experience, ideally in a B2B software, e-commerce, or platform environment
Demonstrated experience owning a defined product area from discovery through delivery — including writing requirements, managing scope, and tracking outcomes
Experience working closely with Engineering and Design teams in an Agile development environment
Track record of building productive working relationships with cross-functional stakeholders and earning credibility through clear communication and reliable execution
Experience using data and customer insights to inform prioritization decisions and evaluate the impact of product changes
Familiarity with defining and tracking product metrics — both leading indicators and business outcomes
Desired
Experience in one or more of the following domains: catalog and search, e-commerce platform, supply chain or order management, customer experience, or internal business systems
Exposure to platforms with large or complex catalogs, configurable products, or high-SKU-count inventory — where search relevance, attribute structure, and navigation design are meaningful product challenges
Familiarity with industrial manufacturing, hardware product development, or engineering procurement workflows — or a genuine interest in developing that knowledge quickly
Experience with operational tooling or business systems (e.g., ERP, CMS, CRM, PIM) and how they interact with customer-facing product experiences
Skills
Strong analytical skills: able to break high-level goals into actionable requirements by synthesizing data, customer insights, and stakeholder input to drive sound product decisions
Clear written and verbal communication: able to write crisp requirements and PRDs, facilitate productive cross-functional discussions, and give stakeholders the information they need to act
Structured thinking: approaches ambiguous problems with a clear process — defining the problem, gathering evidence, framing options, and making a reasoned recommendation
Results orientation: focused on outcomes and impact, not just completing tasks — takes ownership of the success of their work end to end
Collaborative working style: builds relationships across functions with empathy and accountability, and earns credibility through consistency and follow-through
Active and growing AI practice: uses AI tools as a genuine accelerant for drafting, research synthesis, and ideation — and demonstrates intellectual curiosity and learning velocity in developing new AI-assisted workflows as the tooling landscape evolves
Builder mindset: comfortable experimenting with AI-assisted prototyping to communicate product ideas, test assumptions, and accelerate the feedback loop — treating working artifacts as a complement to written documentation, not a replacement for it
Curiosity and learning agility: proactively seeks to understand the business, the customer, and the technical context — and applies new knowledge to improve their product decisions
Perks and Benefits
Competitive medical, dental, and vision insurance
401K plan
Parental leave programs
Paid volunteer days
And much, much more!
Physical Demands
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
While performing the duties of this job, the employee routinely is required to sit; walk; talk and hear; use hands to keyboard, fingers, handle, and feel; stoop, kneel, crouch, twist, crawl, reach, and stretch.
Salary Range: $108,000 to $120,000 per year, depending upon experience

Bring diverse perspectives and experience to our culture and company.
Excel at being part of a strong, empathetic team.
Thrive in an environment emphasizing respect, honesty, collaboration, and growth.
Have an ‘always learning’ mindset that celebrates learning, not just wins.
Help us continue to build a world-class organization that values the contributions of all of our teammates

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. Drive exceptional client growth and empower global trade as a Sales Manager at Flexport.

The Sales team at Flexport is at the forefront of redefining global trade, empowering our clients to navigate complex supply chains with ease. As a Sales Manager, you will lead and mentor a high-performing team of Account Executives who are dedicated to maximizing growth within our existing client base. title: Senior Growth Marketing Manager
description:
About Flexport:
At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.
The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.
About the role
Flexport is hiring a Senior Growth Marketing Manager to do full funnel marketing, including acquisition, expansion, and nurture. This is a hands-on individual contributor role based in San Francisco, reporting to the Director of Growth Marketing.
You’ll manage channels directly, build the tracking and experimentation systems that show what works, and use AI-first workflows to get more done with a lean team. You’ll partner with Brand & Event Marketing, Sales, Sales & Marketing Operations, Customer Success, Product, and Engineering to win new accounts and expand existing ones.
What you’ll do
Channel owner & operator
Manage paid media for acquisition and expansion across Google Ads, LinkedIn, Meta, and YouTube, from campaign structure and bidding to audience development.
Forecast and allocate budget, and decide what to scale or stop based on qualified pipeline and expansion revenue.
Own AEO and SEO: understand ranking factors, fill content gaps, increase share of relevant volume, and stay on top of changes in LLM and agentic search.
Test new channels such as X, Reddit, and creator partnerships, and scale the winners.
Manage our eCommerce store and direct mail, and support events and out-of-home campaigns, in service of brand, awareness, and sales.
Build account-based programs with Sales and Customer Success: define target accounts, use buying signals, and coordinate campaigns with sales outreach and events.
Lead agency and vendor partners with clear briefs and accountability.
Messaging, conversion, and customer marketing
Develop value propositions, differentiation, and persona-based messaging grounded in customer research, competitive positioning, and Product narratives that convert in each channel.
Optimize landing pages and conversion paths, including offers and personalization by segment.
Build customer marketing programs for account expansion and attach: segment customers by usage and whitespace, and run cross-sell and upsell campaigns.
Measurement and experimentation
Build and maintain the tracking foundation: tag management, server-side tracking, conversion APIs, and offline conversion imports that send CRM outcomes back to ad platforms.
Connect spend to pipeline, expansion, and attach revenue using unit economics (CAC, LTV, payback period, contribution margin) and multi-touch and self-reported attribution.
Prove incrementality with holdout and geo-lift tests, and model adstock and diminishing returns to guide channel investment.
Run a documented, hypothesis-driven experimentation program across audiences, bids, offers, creative, and landing pages, with clear readouts.
Use SQL and data science to segment audiences and analyze cohorts, and use reverse ETL to push modeled audiences into ad and lifecycle platforms.
Work with Sales & Marketing Operations on campaign tracking, lead flow to sales handoff, and lead quality and account expansion analysis.
AI-first growth stack
Build AI-first workflows for research, creative, analysis, QA, and reporting, using MCPs, computer use, and automation scripts, with expert human steering on strategy and output.
Build and extend our growth stack and internal tools with code, APIs, command-line tools, and version control, and document each system for reuse.
Track how AI is changing paid media and measurement, and bring what works to the team.
What you’ll bring
You bring paid media expertise, broad channel knowledge, and technical depth.
Experience
7+ years of B2B marketing experience reaching mid-market to enterprise buyers, with ownership of marketing-driven pipeline and account expansion.
5+ years of hands-on paid media experience, managing 7 to 8 figure budgets and scaling spend to the efficient frontier.
2+ years of building with AI, shipping workflows, automations, or internal tools.
Logistics, supply chain, or technology marketing experience (a plus).
Technical depth
Command of tracking, attribution, unit economics, and incrementality methods, including multi-touch models and adstock.
Comfort with querying data warehouses, segmentation, cohort analysis, and reverse ETL, with the judgment to apply data science where it changes a decision.
Working knowledge of A/B testing tools and experimental design.
Operate and be a stakeholder in the sales & marketing stack: CRM, ESP, CMS, account & transaction data, web analytics, and product telemetry.
Craft and judgment
Strong copywriting and conversion optimization skills, from first touch through expansion.
Great taste: you use AI to craft copy and experiences, and you can tell generic output from relevant, on-brand marketing.
AI-first instincts: you know what to automate, what to review, and where your judgment matters.
Clear, confident communication with senior leaders and partner teams.
An organized work style across multiple campaigns and stakeholders.
Mindset
Curiosity about our industry and customers, and the drive to learn ocean and air freight, customs, fulfillment, and the rest of the supply chain.
Adaptable and eager to take on new areas of marketing. Entrepreneurial spirit is a must.

title: Product Manager, Machine Tending
description:
Who we are:
Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.
We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.
Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.
About the team:
The Automation Engineering Team is responsible for delivering robotics-driven automation deployments across a wide range of customer applications. The team partners cross-functionally to translate customer requirements into deployed systems, ensuring solutions are integrated, commissioned, and validated to perform reliably in real manufacturing environments. Automation Engineering works closely with customers, internal technical teams, and external integrators to execute deployments on schedule while maintaining high standards for quality, safety, and repeatability.
About the role:
As Product Manager, Machine Tending, you will own the development, commercialization, and growth of Formic's machine tending offering across both tracks. You will decide which applications we pursue, define standard configurations and pricing, and lead the engineering work that makes them repeatable to deploy.
You will need enough engineering depth to make technical decisions and enough business sense to make commercial ones. You will set direction, get hands-on when needed, and serve as Formic's subject matter expert for the vertical. The goal is an offering Sales can confidently sell, Engineering can consistently deliver, and customers can rely on.
In this role you will:

The ideal candidate combines strong program and people management with a solid understanding of security frameworks (such as NIST CSF and CMMC), risk management, and stakeholder engagement across IT, Legal, business units, and external partners. This role reports to the Sr. Dir, Enterprise Cyber Security and directly manages analysts supporting governance, risk, and awareness functions.
RESPONSIBILITIES

Own the cybersecurity governance program, including the Monthly Cybersecurity Metrics Report and Quarterly Board Dashboard measures.
Define and maintain cybersecurity metrics, KPIs, and KRIs; track program maturity against the NIST CSF; and drive strategic initiatives, risks, and governance commitments to closure.
Coordinate identity governance activities, including monthly AD account reviews, access certifications, and IAM metrics reporting.
Coordinate cybersecurity inputs for the annual cyber insurance renewal and annual Incident Response Plan update and Management tabletop exercise.
Data Security Program Management
Lead data discovery and classification governance across IT, Legal, and business stakeholders, tracking data risk reduction and reporting progress through program metrics.
Third-Party & Supplier Cyber Risk Management
Manage the third-party cyber risk assessment program, including new third-party service reviews, periodic reassessments, critical-supplier (direct and indirect) assessments, and FBIN questionnaires.
Track and drive remediation of third-party and supplier risks and integrate cyber-risk data into governance reporting.
Security Vendor Administration & Operational Oversight
Provide governance administration for cybersecurity vendors (PO creation, invoice processing, DocuSign workflows, renewal tracking) and support legal/contract activities such as NDA/MNDA reviews and security questionnaire responses.
Cybersecurity Policies, Standards & Compliance
Maintain cybersecurity governance documentation, coordinating annual policy and standard updates, approvals, publication and archive.
Support compliance initiatives including SOX controls, CMMC readiness, NIST CSF maturity reporting, SOC 2 assurance, and audit evidence collection and manage governance repositories and control attestations.
Security Awareness Program
Administer the enterprise security awareness program, including annual training, new hire training, National Cybersecurity Awareness Month, quarterly phishing simulations and ad hoc awareness articles on the FBIN intranet.
Leadership & Continuous Improvement
Manage, mentor, and develop analysts supporting governance, risk, and awareness functions.
Partner with cross-functional teams: IT, Legal, connected product, and business units to embed security best practices and continuously improve the maturity, efficiency, and clarity of processes and reporting.

Collaborate: Build partnerships and work collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives.
Communicate Effectively: Develop and deliver multi-mode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences.
Instill Trust: Gain the confidence and trust of others through honesty, integrity, and authenticity.
Builds Effective Teams: Attract, develop, and retain talent to meet current and future organizational needs.
Drives Results: Consistently achieve results, even under challenging circumstances.
Decision Quality: Make sound and timely decisions that keep the organization moving forward.
Plans and Aligns: Plan and prioritize work to meet commitments aligned with organizational goals.
Ensures Accountability: Hold self and others accountable to meet commitments.
Bachelor's degree in Information Security, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
Minimum of 7+ years of overall technology experience, with at least 5+ years in an information security, cybersecurity, or GRC role.
Demonstrated experience owning cybersecurity governance, risk, or compliance programs and producing executive- or board-level reporting.
Working knowledge of security frameworks such as NIST CSF and CMMC, and of enterprise risk and third-party risk management practices.
Experience coordinating security awareness, data security, or identity governance programs across cross-functional stakeholders.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex security topics for technical and non-technical audiences, including leadership.
Strong analytical, organizational, and program-management skills.
PREFERRED :
Prior people-leadership or team-management experience.
Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CISA, or CompTIA Security+.
Experience with GRC and risk platforms and data security tooling.
Familiarity with SOC 2, cyber insurance renewal processes, and audit/assurance coordination.
Experience supporting incident response governance and tabletop exercises.

title: Third Shift Lead Process Technician
description:
Job Description:
ITW's Lakeville, CT facility is seeking an experienced 3rd Shift Lead Process Technician to join our manufacturing team.
We are a clean, modern, fully in-line, highly automated Automotive manufacturing facility utilizing state-of-the-art injection molding equipment, robotics, automated material handling, and advanced vision inspection systems.
The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience with plastic injection molding processes, injection mold tooling, and hot runner systems. Experience with automation and robotic systems is highly desirable.
This position will serve as the technical and operational lead for third-shift manufacturing, providing direction, supervision, and mentorship to machine operators while ensuring production requirements, quality standards, and equipment performance are consistently maintained.
The successful candidate must obtain strong communication skills, possess excellent mechanical aptitude, and demonstrate the ability to independently troubleshoot processing and equipment issues while effectively leading the production team.
This is a hands-on leadership position requiring a balance of technical process knowledge, equipment setup & troubleshooting, production oversight, and team leadership.
Key Responsibilities
Injection Molding Process & Equipment
Set up, start up, and optimize injection molding processes to meet production and quality requirements.
Monitor and maintain process parameters to ensure consistent part quality and production efficiency.
Troubleshoot injection molding process issues, including short shots, flash, dimensional variation, cosmetic defects, and other quality-related concerns.
Demonstrate a strong understanding of injection molds, mold construction, and hot runner systems.
Perform mold changes, process setups, and equipment adjustments as required.
Identify opportunities to improve cycle times, scrap reduction, and improve overall equipment performance.
Work closely with Engineering, Quality, and Maintenance to resolve process and equipment-related issues.
Ensure all production equipment is cleaned, maintained, operating safely and efficiently
Monitor and support Wittmann Battenfeld, Nissei & Toshiba injection molding machines.
Automation & Advanced Manufacturing Technology

Support Wittmann central material feeding systems and auxiliary equipment.
Monitor and troubleshoot automated material handling systems and associated equipment.
Support and troubleshoot Keyence vision inspection systems used to identify part defects and quality-related issues.
Ensure automated inspection systems are functioning properly and identify potential quality concerns.
Work with Maintenance and Engineering to resolve molding & automation-related downtime and equipment issues.
Third Shift Leadership & Production Support
Serve as the technical and operational lead for third-shift manufacturing operations.
Supervise, direct, and mentor machine operators to ensure production expectations are met.
Provide technical guidance and support to operators when processing or equipment issues arise.
Monitor production performance, scrap, downtime, and overall shift efficiency.
Ensure operators follow established work instructions, quality requirements, and safety procedures.
Communicate production concerns, equipment issues, quality problems, and outstanding maintenance needs to the appropriate personnel and incoming shifts.
Maintain accurate production records shift end emails and shift reports.
Escalate issues appropriately and ensure timely resolution of production concerns.
Promote accountability, teamwork, and a positive working environment.
Communication & Documentation
Maintain strong communication with production leadership, Engineering, Quality, Maintenance, and other departments.
Provide detailed and accurate shift handoff information to ensure production continuity.
Utilize Microsoft Office applications, including Excel and Word, for production documentation and reporting.
Utilize Microsoft Outlook for professional communication and coordination.
Maintain accurate records of production issues, downtime. scrap, and process changes.

Perform other related duties and responsibilities as assigned to support manufacturing operations and business needs.
Required Qualifications
Previous 5+ years' experience as a Process Technician in a plastic injection molding manufacturing environment.
Strong understanding of injection molding processes and process optimization.
Experience working with injection molds and hot runner systems.
Demonstrated troubleshooting skills involving molding processes, equipment, and quality-related issues.
Ability to identify and resolve processing issues independently.
Strong mechanical aptitude and hands-on troubleshooting abilities.
Previous experience providing technical direction, leading, supervising, or mentoring production personnel.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and Outlook.
Ability to work independently and make sound decisions in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
Strong commitment to safety, quality, production efficiency, and continuous improvement.

Wittmann Robots: Experience with robotic setup, operation, and troubleshooting.
Wittmann Battenfeld, Nissei, & Toshiba Injection Molding Machines: Experience with machine setup, operation, and process troubleshooting.

Medical Insurance
Dental Insurance
Vision Insurance

description:

The opportunity:
Advancing minimally invasive care requires more than great technology — it requires people who grow with the company, lead with intention, and bring their best to every challenge. The Director, Enterprise Learning will shape how we build capability from the inside out: ensuring every employee, manager, and director has the knowledge, skills, and mindset to perform and grow.
We're looking for someone who sees learning as a business discipline, not a support function. Someone who starts with strategy — understanding where Intuitive is headed and what capabilities will get us there — and works backward to design learning that actually moves the needle. A builder who combines learning design expertise with sharp business judgment, and who knows how to measure whether any of it is working.
This role covers role agnostic enterprise learning below the VP level: individual contributor development, manager learning, director learning, and employee onboarding. It's a broad remit that requires both vision and execution — and a leader who can do both.
What you'll lead:
You'll report directly to the VP, Global Talent and own the strategy, design, and delivery of enterprise-wide learning programs that are connected to business priorities, deliver measurable impact, and built to last. This isn't about building a curriculum library — it's about building capability that shows up in business results.
What this looks like:
Anchor learning to business strategy. Partner closely with HR Business Partners, business leaders, and the broader Talent team to understand where the company is going and what capabilities will be required to get there. Translate that into a multi-year enterprise learning strategy with clear priorities, measurable outcomes, and a coherent point of view on what we build, buy, or curate.
Design learning that works. Lead the design and delivery of learning experiences across the full employee population — from onboarding through director-level development. Apply modern instructional design principles across a range of modalities: in-person, digital, cohort-based, on-demand, and AI-enabled. Prioritize approaches that fit how people actually learn at work.
Own manager and director development. Build and continuously evolve learning programs for managers and directors that are practical, relevant, and grounded in what Intuitive needs from its people leaders. Work closely with HR Business Partners to ensure programs address real capability gaps, not just generic leadership topics.
Deliver a best-in-class onboarding experience. Design and steward an onboarding experience that accelerates time-to-productivity, connects new employees to Intuitive's mission and culture, and sets a strong foundation for long-term engagement and performance.
Make learning measurable. Define clear success metrics for every major program and build the infrastructure to track them. Move beyond attendance and satisfaction scores — connect learning outcomes to performance, retention, and business impact. Use data to make honest calls about what's working and what isn't.
Bring modern learning approaches to life. Stay close to how the learning landscape is evolving — AI-enabled personalization, digital learning platforms, cohort learning, nudge-based reinforcement — and bring the right innovations into Intuitive in ways that are practical and scalable, not just novel.
Build and lead a high-performing team. Lead a team of learning professionals with clarity, high standards, and genuine investment in their development. Create an environment where craft matters, outcomes are tracked, and continuous improvement is the norm.
Partner across HR and the business. Work closely with Talent Management, HR Business Partners, People Analytics, and I&D to ensure enterprise learning is integrated into the broader talent strategy — and that programs reflect and reinforce an inclusive, high-performance culture.
Design and lead manager enablement strategies and programs that equip leaders with the tools, resources, and capabilities to effectively lead and develop their teams.
Design and lead AI enablement and literacy initiatives that build employee confidence, accelerate responsible adoption, and help teams effectively integrate AI into their day-to-day work.
Qualifications
What you'll bring:
Learning strategy and design expertise: Significant experience designing and delivering enterprise learning programs across multiple audiences and modalities — from onboarding through senior individual contributors and people leaders. You understand instructional design deeply and apply it with both rigor and pragmatism.
Business acumen: You think like a business leader. You understand how Intuitive creates value, what's driving the strategy, and how to connect learning investments to business outcomes. You can hold your own in conversations with senior leaders about priorities, trade-offs, and ROI.
Modern learning fluency: Genuine familiarity with the evolving learning landscape — AI-enabled learning tools, digital platforms, cohort-based models, on-demand content strategies, and data-driven personalization. You know what's worth adopting and how to bring it in thoughtfully.
Measurement and outcomes orientation: A track record of defining meaningful success metrics for learning programs and using data to drive decisions. You're not satisfied with completion rates — you want to know whether learning changed behavior and moved business results.
Stakeholder influence: Strong ability to build relationships with and influence senior business leaders and HR partners. You can translate learning strategy into language that resonates with business audiences, and you earn credibility through follow-through and results.
People leadership: You lead with clarity and high standards, invest genuinely in your team's growth, and create an environment where excellent work is the expectation.
Operational excellence: You can manage a complex portfolio of programs, vendors, and priorities without losing sight of quality. You build systems and processes that scale — and you know when to simplify.
Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree in Learning & Development, Organizational Psychology, Instructional Design, or a related field preferred.
12+ years of progressive experience in enterprise learning, with demonstrated success leading learning strategy and design across a large, complex organization.
Experience with AI-enabled learning tools and modern digital learning platforms strongly preferred.
Ability to travel approximately 20% of the time.

Primary Function of Position
Intuitive designs and manufactures highly complex robotic systems for use in minimally invasive surgical applications. Our da Vinci® Surgical Systems design engineering team is committed to utilizing cutting-edge research and technology to develop innovative solutions for our current and next generation surgical robot systems.
In this role, the Mechanical Engineer will be working with multi-disciplinary teams to maintain and improve the design, production, and service of the da Vinci® Surgical System. The ideal candidate will investigate complex problems with electro-mechanical components, manufacturing process, and system performance.  They will identify mechanical design and manufacturing process solutions to improve performance, cost, and reliability. They will also perform the development, documentation, verification, and implementation of these solutions.
Essential Job Duties
·        Collaborate with cross-functional project teams to design, develop, and verify new product design or modifications to robotic or other complex mechanisms.
·        Investigate and determine root cause of both latent and emerging design, manufacturing, or material defects.
·        Develop, design, test, document, and implement solutions to the root causes identified for improved performance and reliability.
·        Perform various types of detailed engineering analyses (tolerance stack, process simulation, structural FEA) to ensure fit/form/function of complex tooled parts.
·        Create formal documentation, perform verification testing, and lead implementation of design solutions.
Required Skills and Experience
·        Self-driven with the ability to excel in a high-energy, small, focused team environment, to maintain a strong sense of shared responsibility and shared reward, and to make work fun and interesting.
·        Proficiency in CAD (Solidworks preferred), including complex assemblies, GD&T, and functional dimensioning.
·        Experience with machine design, preferably robot or mechanical systems design experience. Surgical product experience is a plus
·        Proven proficiency at failure analysis
·        Demonstrated mechanical design and analysis skills, including statics, dynamics, kinematics, strength of materials and stress analysis
·        Comfortable with all phases of the product development lifecycle including design, implementation, debug, verification, qualification, and transfer to Manufacturing.
·        Excellent communication (written, oral) and interpersonal skills, and ability to communicate effectively.
Required Education and Training
Minimum of 5 years related experience with a Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Robotics or equivalent; or 3 years experience and a Master’s degree; or a PhD without experience
Preferred Skills and Experience
·        Surgical or medical device product experience is a plus.
·        Preferred to have demonstrated effective collaboration with cross-functional teams like system analysts, clinical, human factors, industrial design, interaction design, etc.
·        Comfortable using Matlab, Python, or similar software
·        Experience with designing hardware products in a regulated industry is desired; comfort with concepts of design input, design output, traceability, and risk analysis
·        Regulatory agency experience including UL, CE, and FDA approval processes

description:

If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Position Summary
The Senior Program Manager, People Experience & Operations is a trusted partner to the Vice President of PXO and a key integrator across People Services, People Technology & Digital Employee Experience, and People Analytics. This role combines the judgment and executive partnership of a chief of staff with the discipline of a portfolio program manager and the ownership of a hands-on operator.
Working through program and project managers across the broader HR organization, this person builds a cohesive view of the most important work: what is underway, how initiatives connect, where decisions or resources are needed, and what could put delivery at risk. They establish clear operating rhythms and scalable ways of working, while directly leading select cross-functional priorities. The role is not intended to replace the PMs accountable for individual projects. It makes their work easier to connect, prioritize, and communicate at a leadership level.
Key Responsibilities
Portfolio Integration, Visibility & Governance
·   Partner with PMs, functional leaders, and the broader HR PMO to consolidate existing project plans and updates into a decision-ready view of the PXO portfolio, without duplicating project-level ownership or reporting.
·   Map dependencies, milestones, decisions, risks, resource constraints, and ownership across initiatives; identify collisions or sequencing issues early and drive the right conversations to resolve them.
·   Establish lightweight standards and practical routines for intake, portfolio reviews, escalation, decision logs, and follow-through; improve data quality and accountability without creating unnecessary process.
·   Translate portfolio information into concise executive dashboards and narratives that distinguish what is on track, what needs attention, and where VP or leadership intervention will make a difference.
Executive Partnership & Operating Rhythm
·   Serve as a trusted thought partner to the VP, connecting the dots across teams, anticipating needs, pressure-testing options, and translating priorities into clear next steps.
·   Run an effective leadership operating cadence: staff meetings, agendas, pre-reads, decision tracking, quarterly priorities, leadership offsites, and follow-up on commitments.
·   Develop clear, audience-appropriate briefings, presentations, communications, and recommendations for senior HR, IT, Finance, and other stakeholders.
·   Support planning and prioritization by bringing visibility to commitments, capacity, headcount and budget dependencies, and trade-offs; partner with accountable functional and Finance leaders rather than assuming their ownership.
Complex Programs & Special Initiatives
·   Personally lead selected high-priority initiatives that span teams or lack a natural owner, from framing the problem and aligning stakeholders through execution and measurable outcomes.
·   Build practical plans, clarify decision rights, surface blockers with recommendations, and drive action across matrixed partners without relying on formal authority.
·   Help leaders navigate change, coordinate communications and handoffs, and turn ambiguous or fast-moving requirements into repeatable, scalable approaches.
Employee Experience, Connection & Communication
·   Help shape and deliver purposeful PXO all-hands, team forums, recognition practices, and leadership events that strengthen connection across a global organization.
·   Partner with leaders to turn employee survey and listening insights into meaningful actions, track commitments, and close the feedback loop.
·   Bring care and consistency to team communications and operating rituals so people feel informed, recognized, and connected to the broader purpose of the work.
What You Bring
·   8+ years of experience in complex program or portfolio management, business operations, enterprise transformation, or a chief of staff–type role, with evidence of outcomes across functions.
·   Experience working with multiple project or program managers to synthesize a portfolio view, navigate cross-project dependencies, and support executive decisions. You can see the system without losing the details.
·   Excellent judgment, discretion, and executive communication: you simplify complexity, bring options rather than just problems, and know when to act independently or escalate.
·   A builder mindset. You create structure where it is missing, improve processes without adding bureaucracy, and turn ambiguous needs into practical solutions that last.
·   Exceptional follow-through, organization, and ownership, paired with curiosity, humility, empathy, a positive and collaborative approach, and an instinct for bringing people together.
·   Confidence influencing senior stakeholders without formal authority, handling confidential information responsibly, and staying composed when priorities shift.
·   An AI-forward or AI-curious mindset: you proactively explore appropriate AI and automation tools to improve synthesis, reporting, workflows, and productivity, while exercising strong judgment about accuracy, privacy, and data security.
·   Proficiency in presentation, spreadsheet, collaboration, and project/portfolio management tools; bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
Preferred Experience
·   Experience in People/HR functions, HR technology, enterprise services, or a global matrixed or regulated business.
·   Familiarity with platforms such as Workday, ServiceNow, Qualtrics, Smartsheet, or equivalent tools, as well as change management or employee listening programs.
·   Experience supporting VP-level leadership, including operating reviews, executive communications, and cross-functional annual planning; relevant PMP training is a plus.
What Success Looks Like
The VP and PXO leadership have a clear, trusted view of the portfolio and can quickly see key dependencies, trade-offs, owners, risks, and decisions. PMs across HR have a collaborative partner who connects their work rather than recreating it. Important initiatives move forward, commitments are followed through, and the team benefits from clear communication, thoughtful recognition, and consistent operating practices. Above all, this person is known for sound judgment, initiative, reliability, and making both leaders and colleagues more effective.

title: Staff Mechanical Engineer
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of the Position
Intuitive Surgical designs and manufactures highly complex mechanical systems for use in surgery. These systems include both capital equipment and “consumables” in the form of surgical instruments and accessories. The Staff Mechanical Engineer for Instrument and Accessory Advanced Product Development will be a member of a small team responsible for exploring and developing early product concepts and technologies that will help feed the da Vinci product pipeline. The successful candidate will lead early assessment, design, development, sourcing, testing, and integration of novel concepts for instrument and accessory related products.
The candidate will help to identify and evaluate new candidate technologies, establish design requirements and create novel designs to meet customer needs, work with suppliers and other outside companies to realize viable technical solutions, and refine designs for transfer to the New Product Development organization. He/she/they must excel in a high-energy team environment and be capable of creative problem solving when faced with the time pressures and incomplete information typical of early-stage product development. The successful candidate must have outstanding technical depth in relevant areas and be as comfortable collaborating and leading across organizational boundaries as they are working independently.
Essential Job Duties
Work within cross-functional project teams to create, evaluate, and prove out new product architectures and refine them for hand off to new Product Development
Collaborate with subject matter experts to understand the clinical, usability, and other needs of users of da Vinci systems as they relate to surgical instruments and accessories. Assist with market research and surgeon discussions around concepts, approaches, and procedures
Develop technical requirements for designs based on an understanding of customer needs, commercial objectives (e.g. cost of goods), regulatory requirements, and feasibility constraints
Perform conceptual design, detailed design, analytical modeling, prototyping, data analysis, and troubleshooting of novel instruments and accessories for the da Vinci robotic surgical system
Develop and perform early design verification and validation testing, with assistance from other functions as needed
Assist with clinical evaluation of prototypes by supporting bench, ex-vivo, and in-vivo laboratory testing
Provide written protocols, reports, and presentations related to design activities on an ongoing basis
Refine and document product designs as needed to support successful transfer into the new product development organization
Technical leadership
Act as technical lead on product development projects
Mentor and train less experienced engineers in the art of product development and mechanical design
Review mechanical engineering designs of other Intuitive engineers in both a formal and informal capacity
Lead or assist other design engineers through brainstorming, detailed reviews, and collaborative problem-solving, resulting in compelling product architectures
Develop and manage relationships with key partners and suppliers
Assess technologies from outside entities for potential licensing and adaptation to the da Vinci product line
Identify, test, and report on new materials, manufacturing processes, and technologies that could benefit existing products or enable new product designs
Provide detailed input to project planning, including objectives, budgets, staffing, schedules, milestones, etc.
Make recommendations to senior management about the direction, activities, and staffing of ongoing projects, as well as recommendations and proposals for new product/project opportunities
Identify resource gaps and make recommendations to address issues and prioritize
Other Functions
Document, prepare and review patent submissions
May supervise or direct the activities of others
Required Skills and Experience
Twelve (12) years of experience in mechanical product design, or eight (8) years with MS, five (5) with PhD
Extensive experience taking products from concept to production. Medical and/or regulated product experience highly preferred
Familiarity with all phases of the product development lifecycle including design, implementation, debug, verification, validation, qualification, and transfer
Understanding of mechatronics, robotics, and servo-controlled systems strongly preferred. Experience developing software control algorithms a plus
Proven ability to apply the basic laws of physics to understand and achieve quick and reliable solutions to engineering problems
Exceptional mechanical aptitude and visual thinking skills
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills such as finite element analysis, statistics, and experimental designs
Experience with and knowledge of a wide range of prototyping processes, both rapid and conventional with a variety of metallic and non-metallic materials
Excellent written and verbal communication and presentation skills. Ability to present to a wide range of audiences, including senior executives
Ability to interface with customers and potential business partners in a highly professional manner
Proven ability to work well in a team environment and drive individual projects. Experience managing external partners, suppliers, and small project teams
Proficiency using CAD to create and document mechanical designs. SolidWorks preferred
Proficient with hands-on development work for electromechanical products:
Operating standard machine shop equipment for prototyping (mill, lathe, etc.)
Techniques for rapidly fabricating proof-of-concept and functional prototypes
Standard mechanical and electrical measurement and test equipment
Required Education and Training
BS (Mechanical Engineering or related engineering field) required, MS or PhD preferred
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience and skills in design of high volume (e.g. injection molded, MIM) components, and design for reliability and manufacturability strongly preferred

Primary Function of Position
The DaVinci Specialist (DVS) will provide expert clinical & technical support, build, customize and coordinate education & training to physicians, nurses, and hospital staff on the use of DaVinci surgery, devices and therapies. This role partners closely with the sales team, specifically the Clinical Sales Representative and Clinical Sales Manager, to ensure safe and effective product adoption and quality control while driving positive patient outcomes.
The DaVinci Specialist is a dedicated program execution & clinical education partner for hospitals running a da Vinci robotic surgery program.   Based on its expertise, this role focuses on identifies and tailors the nature and extent of staff in-servicing, day-to-day program execution, technology onboarding and operational support, communicating identified needs to hospital OR operations and leadership. The DVS will work alongside the daVinci Clinical Sales Representative .
Essential Job Duties
Collaboration & Field Partnership (Within a CSM Team)
Partner with the local CSR/CSM and cross-functional business partners to create, own, scale and execute best practices and deployment of ecosystem resources.
Lead account support plans that drive safe program execution and increase customer autonomy over time, including setting objectives, timelines and resources for relevant customers, in consultation with CSR/CSM.
Identify, solicit and provide field feedback and customer insights to internal teams to improve training, support resources, and customer experience.
Support adoption of digital solutions by helping customers build comfort and capability through in-servicing and troubleshooting.
Clinical & Technical Support
Identify and provide on-site, non-scrubbed operating room support for procedures utilizing the da Vinci Surgical System and associated technologies.
Support OR teams with room readiness and procedural workflow, including system setup support, docking workflow support, and intraoperative troubleshooting.
Serve as a clinical product expert to help ensure optimal, safe system use and adherence to applicable IFUs, hospital policies, and safety protocols.
Motivate and support adoption of advanced instruments and accessories by ensuring teams understand proper setup, handling, and intended use.
Partner with and promote consistent readiness and workflow by supporting day-to-day execution of the robotic program, coordinating with OR leadership, nursing, SPD/sterile processing, and biomedical teams.
Assist with operational support activities such as facilitating appropriate internal handoffs for service needs.
Ensure the right stakeholders are aligned (OR, SPD, biomed, IT) for successful day-to-day operation and new technology onboarding to help reduce friction.
Maintain accurate internal documentation of support activities per company process (e.g., case support notes, training records, service/escalation tracking).
Training & Education (Care Team Enablement)
Determine the need for, customize and deliver customer-specific hands-on training and in-services to nurses, surgical technologists, SPD teams, and other care team members on safe and effective use of da Vinci platforms and associated technologies.
Support onboarding and education for new users through structured training touchpoints (e.g., new staff orientation, refresher training, workflow standardization).
Lead new site start-ups by identifying and delivering onboarding programs and coordinating training logistics with the CSR/CSM and hospital stakeholders.
Support new technology installs by coordinating readiness activities and providing post-install education to care teams.
Act as a resource for ongoing education, product updates, and workflow optimization.
Escalation & Customer Issue Management
Analyze and leverage utilization, turnover, and other relevant case data to recommend operational changes to customers
Provide first-line support and expertise for common setup and workflow issues during live cases and training sessions.
Identify, resolve and where necessary escalate issues appropriately to internal partners (e.g., Technical Support, Field Service, Clinical/Medical counterparts).
Market & Clinical Insights
Collect and communicate customer feedback and experiences to clinical counterparts and internal business partners.  Prioritizing, distilling and reporting relevant customer feedback, in real time.
Stay up to date on clinical literature, competitive products, and evolving treatment guidelines.
Assist in clinical trial support when required.
Assist in field action activities when necessary.

Experience: 2+ years in an operating room-related role
Clinical experience is preferred.
Experience as a robotics coordinator, surgical assistant, and/or surgical nurse plus industry experience strongly preferred.
Understanding of soft tissue anatomy & procedures.
Exhibit a working knowledge of typical hospital policies.
Excellent communication, teaching, and interpersonal skills.
Strong problem solving and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to work in high-pressure environments (managing multiple ORs) and coordination of multiple tasks at one time.
Adaptability to evolving technologies and complex procedures.
Team oriented with a commercial mindset.
Willingness to travel up to 40%. Primary travel will be within a CSM team.
Ability to travel within a Clinical Sales Manager team geography, supporting multiple hospitals.
Flexibility to support early starts, after-hours cases, and weekend procedures based on customer need and territory utilization.

Ability to stand for extended periods and provide in-person case support within an operating room (OR) environment, which includes pushing, pulling, lifting and squatting.

title: Corporate Recruiter

Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Headquartered in Chicago, we develop, own, and operate large scale projects that power communities and support the energy future.
Invenergy follows a hybrid schedule, working in office Monday through Thursday and remotely on Fridays if work permits.
This position will be open for application for at least 3 calendar days from the posting date. This position will remain open for application based on business need, which may be before or after the 3-day posting window.
Job Description
Position Overview
The Corporate Recruiter supports the growth of our business by leading the full life cycle recruiting process for corporate positions. The Corporate Recruiter will partner closely with hiring leaders and their teams to build recruiting strategies, attract and assess talent, and deliver an excellent candidate experience.
Responsibilities
Lead the full life cycle recruiting process for corporate positions
Partner with business leaders and hiring managers to define role requirements, hiring priorities, and interview plans; provide consultative guidance and timely communication.
Develop and execute sourcing and recruiting strategies; share market insights and recommend adjustments to improve candidate flow and quality.
Provide a superior candidate experience throughout the end-to-end recruiting process including candidate review, phone screens, interview scheduling/coordination and offer
Screen and assess candidates, coordinate interviews, and manage the offer process while ensuring a consistent, high-quality candidate experience.
Represent Invenergy’s employee value proposition in a compelling, consistent manner to candidates and stakeholders.
Maintain accurate documentation in the applicant tracking system (ATS) and support reporting on recruiting progress and results.
Use sound, professional judgment in all interactions and foster an equal employment opportunity environment.
Participate in talent acquisition initiatives and process improvement projects
Support career fairs, networking events, presentations, and local/community outreach as needed
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor’s Degree

description:

With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Job Description
Position Overview
The Director of Internal Controls will build and lead a practical, business-focused enterprise internal control and risk management program that supports Invenergy’s continued growth. This role will partner directly with leaders across finance, accounting, technology, legal, compliance, development, construction, and operations to identify and assess significant risks, establish scalable controls, strengthen process documentation, and promote clear ownership and accountability.
The Director will be a hands-on leader who can set the strategy, develop the program, and work alongside the business to provide practical, risk-based guidance and maintain an effective, sustainable control environment as the organization evolves.
Responsibilities
Build and lead a formal annual enterprise risk assessment process that identifies significant risks across the organization, evaluates their relative likelihood and impact, and maps the controls intended to mitigate those risks.
Incorporate fraud risk into the annual assessment, including potential fraud schemes, incentives and opportunities, management override, and the preventive and detective controls needed to address those risks.
Maintain a practical, formally documented risk and internal control inventory that identifies each objective, associated risk, control activity, owner, and frequency, and ensure it is updated as the business, systems, risks, and processes change.
Ensure key processes and controls are supported by approved, usable procedures that define the control objective, execution steps, frequency, preparer, reviewer, exception handling, escalation, and required evidence.
Develop a scalable internal control framework and operating model that reflects Invenergy’s ownership structure, business complexity, growth plans, and risk profile.
Work directly with business and functional leaders to establish clear accountability and design controls that are effective, efficient, and integrated into day-to-day operations.
Perform and oversee periodic reviews of control design and operation, identify gaps, agree on practical corrective actions with management, and monitor remediation through completion.
Challenge existing processes constructively and identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate, and strengthen controls while supporting speed, accountability, and business growth.
Establish and maintain formal internal audit procedures, including a risk-based annual audit plan, scoping, planning, fieldwork, sampling, testing, documentation, quality review, reporting, issue rating, management responses, remediation follow-up, and escalation.
Maintain appropriate independence and objectivity for internal audit activities and coordinate efficiently with external auditors, legal, compliance, technology, and other assurance partners.
Provide concise, decision-useful reporting to senior management and other governance stakeholders on key risks, control coverage, audit results, open issues, remediation progress, and emerging concerns.
Serve as a trusted advisor to management on new initiatives, acquisitions, systems, and process changes so that appropriate controls are considered early and scaled to the underlying risk.
Build risk and control awareness across the organization through practical training, clear guidance, and regular communication with control owners.
Develop the internal controls function over time, including setting priorities, managing resources, developing talent, and maintaining a multi-year roadmap aligned with the company’s needs.
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree or higher in accounting.
10+ years of progressive experience in internal controls, internal audit, enterprise risk management, compliance, public accounting, or a related field, including experience working directly with senior business leaders.
Demonstrated experience building or improving risk assessments, risk and control inventories, process documentation, and internal audit or control monitoring programs.
Strong understanding of risk and internal control principles, including fraud risk, control design, issue evaluation, remediation, and managing controls through business and system change.
Proven ability to operate strategically and tactically, build a function from the ground up, and translate risk concepts into practical processes that business teams can own and sustain.
Strong judgment, curiosity, leadership, project management, and written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to succeed in an entrepreneurial, fast-paced, and collaborative environment with evolving priorities, limited bureaucracy, and a high degree of personal accountability.
Eligible to work in the United States without the need for employer visa sponsorship now or in the future.
Preferred Qualifications
CPA, CIA, CISA, or other relevant professional certification preferred.
Big four public accounting experience preferred.
Experience applying COSO or similar frameworks in a practical, risk-based manner appropriate for a growing, operationally complex organization.
Experience in the energy, power generation, infrastructure, construction, or renewable energy industries.
Experience with governance, risk, and compliance tools, data analytics, technology-enabled controls, and control automation.

description:
Job Description
The EHS Manager will be responsible for the execution of the EHS strategy, culture and performance, overseeing Operational Risk Management (ORM) processes that include Safety and Health, Environment, Business Continuity, Facility Security, Asset Conservation, Department of Transportation (DOT) and Pandemic Planning. The primary purpose of this position is to ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state and local laws and regulations, and to ensure KraftHeinz EHS policies/procedures and processes are understood and sustained across the plant by employees, visitors and contractors. In addition, this position requires foresight and planning: actively identifying and communicating operational risks within the factory, and partnering with others to develop plans and business strategies to mitigate those risks.

Own and execute EHS strategies that align with corporate objectives and aspirations

Ability to build and execute Strategy and Initiatives

Develop and maintain new and current processes and tools to ensure sustained compliance with all Federal, State, and local EHS regulations

Drive continuous improvement, capability and culture across the plant towards best in class performance and a zero incident mindset

Our Company             The Kraft Heinz Company is the fifth largest food and beverage company in the world, with eight $1 billion+ brands and global sales of approximately $25 billion. We are a globally trusted producer of delicious foods for 150 years, and we provide high quality, great taste and nutrition for all eating occasions whether at home, in restaurants or on-the-go. The Kraft Heinz Company manufactures and markets food and beverage products in the United States, Canada, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Latin America, Australia and throughout Asia-Pacific. Our products include condiments and sauces, cheese and dairy, meals, meats, refreshment beverages, coffee, and other grocery products, as well as infant and nutrition products.

description:
Job Description:
Continuous Improvement (CI) Specialist
Columbus, OH
Multiple Opportunities
Are you ready to champion a zero-loss culture on the manufacturing shop floor? As a Continuous Improvement (CI) Specialist, you will be the driving force behind loss elimination, providing crucial leadership across all MSE pillars—with a dedicated focus on advancing Autonomous Maintenance (AM) and Focused Improvement (FI). In this role, you won't just manage processes; you will empower and upskill frontline operating teams, elevating their technical mastery of process control while partnering directly with Daily Management System (DMS) owners to lock in sustainable operational excellence.
The Continuous Improvement (CI) Specialist is responsible for leading loss elimination and is critical to support all MSE pillars, specifically AM and FI. The CI Specialist is expected to develop the operating teams’ technical understanding and mastery of process control, area operation and to support all Daily Management Systems (DMS) owners.
What are we looking for?
Minimum:
Bachelor’s in Engineering, Supply, Business, or technical field of study or 4 years’ experience in manufacturing with TPM (MSE) participation
3+ years of hands-on experience working within a manufacturing environment utilizing Autonomous Maintenance (AM) and Focused Improvement (FI) pillars.
Direct experience executing and maintaining daily Autonomous Maintenance Daily Management Systems, specifically Centerline (CL), Clean, Inspect, Lubricate (CIL), and Abnormality Handling (AH).
Proficiency in basic problem-solving tools (such as the 5 Whys, Fishbone diagrams, and basic Root Cause Analysis) with a track record of applying them to eliminate line losses.
Demonstrated ability to collect, interpret, and report operational and machine performance data.
Experience actively participating in daily operational tier meetings (such as FMOS tier meetings) and communicating technical action plans clearly to a diverse team.
Highly proficient in SAP and the Microsoft Office Suite (specifically Excel, PowerPoint, and Word) to support administrative, operational, and presentation workflows.
Preferred:
Extensive experience and deep subject matter expertise in Autonomous Maintenance (AM) and Focused Improvement (FI) pillars.
Proven success in AM and FI pillars, with a documented history of designing and executing line-level training and coaching programs for operators and technical teams.
Experience facilitating Area Loss Analysis and successfully creating and driving 90-day to 1-year area improvement roadmaps that deliver measurable reduction in losses.
Mastery of advanced problem-solving tools (such as Six Sigma Green/Black Belt methodologies, FMEA, or advanced RCPS) to solve complex, chronic chronic losses.
Proven capability to operate effectively within an operational "triad" (partnering proactively with Shift Managers and Technical Owners) to drive a zero-loss culture on the shop floor.
Expert-level understanding of both PDCA and SDCA cycles to systematically transition from standardizing baseline performance to driving continuous improvement.
What are the job responsibilities?
Serve as the on-site Subject Matter Expert (SME) for continuous improvement methodologies, with a dedicated focus on driving the Autonomous Maintenance (AM) and Focused Improvement (FI) pillars, while proactively training and upskilling frontline team members.
Actively lead performance discussions during daily Factory Management Operating System (FMOS) meetings by presenting machine-level health metrics, defining immediate action plans, and communicating completed recovery work.
Facilitate and take full ownership of the Area Loss Analysis process; systematically gather, analyze, and translate line data into high-impact 90-day and 1-year continuous improvement roadmaps.
Own and govern the daily execution of AM Daily Management Systems (DMS)—including Centerline (CL), Clean-Inspect-Lubricate (CIL), Abnormality Handling (AH), and 5S—as well as the line's Changeover DMS to ensure robust PDCA (Plan-Do-Check-Act) and SDCA (Standardize-Do-Check-Act) cycles.
Actively champion and support Integrated Work Team (IWT) initiatives, aligning efforts across AM and Planned Maintenance (PM) activities to maximize line reliability.
Lead structured, cross-functional problem-solving initiatives to eradicate chronic area losses, utilizing both foundational and advanced Root Cause Problem Solving (RCPS) toolsets.
Act as an internal coach, empowering and developing shop floor associates' problem-solving capabilities to resolve baseline issues autonomously.
Operate as a key member of the shift "triad" (Operations, Technical, and Quality/MSE), providing proactive, real-time support to day-to-day manufacturing operations.

Accelerator, a global Division of Mars Snacking, is on the front line of unlocking growth across high-potential categories and brands to fuel what’s next for Snacking. This is a project-based, 24-month assignment for a food safety expert who thrives on driving change and innovation. We're looking for a specialist to lead critical laboratory and technology programs aimed at making our products safer, optimizing our processes, and reducing verification costs. In this role, you will be the bridge between cutting-edge technology and our manufacturing reality, taking new analytical methods from the lab bench and deploying them in the field. You'll also partner directly with our Supply Quality Assurance (SQA) team, acting as a microbiological expert for high-risk ingredient suppliers and serving as the authorized witness for critical food safety dispositions. This is your chance to make a significant, measurable impact on how we ensure quality across the Accelerator division.
What You’ll Do (Key Responsibilities)
Lead Laboratory & Technology Programs:   Manage the network of third-party labs, optimize testing practices, and serve as the SME for internal laboratories. Validate and deploy new food safety technologies and analytical methods (e.g., CleanWorks, Gene-UP).
Drive Supplier Quality:   Provide microbiological expertise and support SQA during audits of high-risk supplier manufacturing sites. Partner with SQA on Material Risk Assessments (MRA), ingredient specifications, and Inbound Verification Testing (IVT).
Manage Quality Incidents & Risk:   Provide PRIMP support by managing escalated testing and leading laboratory investigations. Support the division's quality risk management activities, ensuring risks are documented and tracked in the Archer platform.
Oversee Data & Training:   Oversee the trending of finished product test data, leading quarterly reviews to provide recommendations for optimization. Develop and deliver training to build food safety and laboratory capability among internal teams.
Act as Authorized Witness:   Serve as the authorized witness for the disposition of food safety-critical materials, ensuring compliance with Mars corporate standards.
What We’re Looking For
A Lab & Technology Expert:   Advanced knowledge of microbiological and allergen hazards, analytical methods, and laboratory quality systems (e.g., ISO 17025).
A Project-Driven Doer:   Proven experience managing projects, from pilot trials and data validation to the full deployment of new technologies in a manufacturing environment.
A Supplier Quality Partner:   Experience auditing operational processes, particularly for high-risk ingredient suppliers, and a strong understanding of MRAs and IVT.
An Independent Collaborator:   The ability to work with a high degree of autonomy while building strong relationships with SQA, R&D, and external lab partners to get things done.
Qualifications
Education:   Bachelor’s degree in Food Science, Microbiology, Biology, or a closely related field.
Experience:   7+ years of experience in food manufacturing and laboratory quality systems.
Certifications:   HACCP or related certification required. Certification and experience auditing operational processes required.
Location:   Based in Chicago, IL or Battle Creek, MI.
Travel:   Ability to travel (~30%) to labs and manufacturing sites.

As the Business Planner, Azure Container Services and Developer Innovation , you will play a critical role in shaping how Microsoft monetizes and grows some of Azure’s most important container, developer, and emerging AI services.
AI agents are moving from pilot to production, and they need a secure, scalable place to run. On Azure, that place is increasingly containers. Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) is Azure's managed Kubernetes platform, widely adopted by enterprises to run applications at scale, and it is increasingly central to how organizations run AI workloads.
