title: Critical Environment Technician (Night Shift)
description:
Overview
As a  Critical Environment Technician (CET)  in Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) team, you will help to maintain the critical infrastructure that keeps our datacenters up and running. This could be anything from performing basic monitoring and inspection, performing various types of maintenance, participating in equipment troubleshooting, enforcing all safety and security requirements, and developing methods of operating procedures (MOPs) and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Critical Environment Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties.
Responsibilities
Critical Environment Culture
Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance Provides necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site based on the appropriate procedure levels of risk (LOR). Takes part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Recognizes circumstances when to stop supplier/vendor work to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates per appropriate LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Reviews and completes appropriate work orders to support approval of vendor supplier field service reports or invoices.
Performs troubleshooting of equipment and systems independently within their trained discipline(s). Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Communicates and/or escalates troubleshooting issues or anomalies with assistance from more experienced colleagues. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment works within disciplines they have been trained.
Prepares and submits required reports (e.g., turnover, preventative maintenance [PM]) as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates. Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for appropriately leveled procedures to ensure safe and reliable execution. Documents completed work using approved tools and procedural templates for more experienced technician review. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments.
Develops an understanding of method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Coordinates activities and associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities.
Performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs (e.g., basic replacements, changing of parts) for specific disciplines and equipment for which they have been trained, following methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) with minimal supervision - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Performs lower level maintenance with minimal supervision, and may resolve high level issues with support from more experienced colleagues. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Maintains all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance.
Equipment and Systems Operations Safely responds to and stabilizes abnormal conditions within the required timeframes for various abnormal facility events within data center with minimal supervision, utilizing emergency operating procedures (EOPs). Gathers necessary information and participates in the creation of incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur. Assists in developing emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Assists in providing emergency monitoring response to irregular or malfunctioning conditions.
Works on tasks (e.g., making rounds, initial assessments on equipment performance) as assigned with varying levels of supervision, sometime minimal. Supports senior colleagues as an assistant. Builds knowledge in operating equipment and systems within a set discipline (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls). Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work. Tracks hours for performed tasks within applicable task management systems. Adds required data, documents, logs changes, and upkeeps procedures related to building management systems and reports. Properly signals spare equipment and parts utilization within maintenance work orders.
Performs monitoring physical inspection of critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds for unsafe or abnormal conditions. Understands critical system alarms for single discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) within the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify critical alarms. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems.
Physical Requirements Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting 50lbs / 22.5kg. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg. with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
Working Conditions Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
As indicated above, this role has a travel requirement of up to 25% which means you may be required to travel, from time to time, as part of this role.
As indicated above,   have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.

High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent.

The Platform Systems Engineering (PSE) team is seeking a Principal AI Back-End Network Systems Lead  to serve as the technical lead and end-to-end product development owner for Back End Network across both scale-up and scale-out. The role will lead the product from requirements and architecture through design, integration, validation, manufacturing readiness, deployment, and fleet learning - spanning silicon, network adapters, switches, interconnects, optics/electrical channels, and the fabric as a complete system.
The successful candidate will bring deep expertise in one or more AI/ML scale-up or scale-out networking domains and the product-level thinking to connect decisions across the full system. This lead will work from physical and data-link technologies through network and transport behavior to collectives, workloads, modeling, observability, and datacenter deployment, creating clarity across architecture, execution, quality, performance, reliability, power, cost, and schedule.
#azure #MAIA #AI/ML #Networking #ScaleUp #ScaleOut
Responsibilities
End-to-End Product Ownership & Architecture
Own the Back End Network product definition and execution plan across scale-up and scale-out, from customer/workload needs and product requirements through architecture, development, qualification, deployment, and fleet learning.
Translate AI training and inference requirements into measurable system targets for bandwidth, latency, scale, collective efficiency, reliability, availability, serviceability, power, thermal behavior, cost, security, and schedule.
Make and drive cross-system architecture decisions, interface contracts, feature priorities, and risk tradeoffs; maintain clear ownership, milestones, entry/exit criteria, and product readiness metrics.
Lead NUDD (new, unique, different, and difficult) technology assessments, prototypes, make/buy/partner decisions, and mitigation plans for the highest product risks.
Scale-Up/Scale-Out Systems, Silicon, Switch & Fabric
Lead architecture and integration across accelerator and networking silicon, NICs/DPUs, PHYs/retimers, switch ASICs, switches, cables/backplanes, optics, and fabric topology.
Define scalable scale-up and scale-out architectures, including topology, radix, reach, link speeds, routing, path diversity, oversubscription, failure domains, and resiliency.
Drive silicon, board, switch, firmware, network operating system, and fabric requirements so that components operate as one high-performance and serviceable product.
Partner with silicon, switch, optical, cable, connector, system, manufacturing, and supplier teams to deliver designs from concept through production and datacenter integration.
Optical/Electrical & Cross-Layer Integration
Oversee electrical and optical technologies for high-speed links, including signal integrity, SerDes/PHY, link training, FEC, reach, power, thermal, mechanical, manufacturability, and interoperability tradeoffs.
Drive end-to-end behavior across the relevant OSI layers - physical, data link, network, and transport - and the system/runtime interfaces above them.
Define and validate Ethernet/RDMA or other scale-up/scale-out protocol behavior, including flow control, congestion control, QoS, routing, packet loss/recovery, telemetry, and security.
Ensure hardware, firmware, drivers, network operating systems, management software, orchestration, and datacenter operations are aligned to common specifications and concepts of operation.
Collectives, Workloads, Modeling & Performance
Connect network architecture to distributed AI workloads, parallelism strategies, traffic patterns, and collective operations such as all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter, and all-to-all.
Establish analytical and simulation models for topology, bandwidth, latency, congestion, failure behavior, collective efficiency, workload scaling, power, and cost.
Use models, emulation, prototypes, and lab/fleet data to predict bottlenecks, guide design choices, set performance budgets, and validate architectural assumptions.
Partner with workload, collective-communication, compiler/runtime, and application teams to co-optimize the network and improve job completion time and cluster efficiency.

The International Customer Success Organization (iCSU) mission is to deliver and scale world-class customer success services for Microsoft’s most strategic, innovative, complex, and globally operating customers worldwide. We help customers to accelerate business value through differentiated customer experiences that leverage Microsoft’s products and services, ignited by our people and culture. We drive cross-company alignment and execution, ensuring that we consistently exceed customers’ expectations in every interaction, whether in-product, digital, or human-centered.
We are looking for a Senior Cloud Solution Architect, Cloud & AI Business Solutions  to help global customers turn their most ambitious Cloud & AI ideas into production outcomes on Azure. Whether your depth is in data platforms or in AI applications and agents, you will partner with customers to build unified, governed, AI-ready data estates and to move AI apps and agents from experimentation to production. In this customer-facing role, you will lead technical engagements across architecture design, proofs of concept, pilots, and production milestones using Azure AI Foundry, Microsoft Fabric, Azure Databricks, GitHub, and related Azure data and app services. You will use repeatable IP, Factory, Unified VAS, and Acceleration Programs to deliver scalable outcomes, generate incremental pipeline, and improve time-to-value for mission-critical workloads. This role is flexible in that you can work up to 100% from home.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
Engage customer IT and business leaders to understand their data, application, agent, and AI priorities; define success measures and design secure, scalable solutions that drive measurable business value and production adoption.
Lead hands-on architecture, proofs of concept, pilots, and production deployments, including Cloud Acceleration Factory engagements, across AI-ready data platforms, analytics, databases, AI applications, and agents.
Own end-to-end technical delivery results, ensuring completeness and accuracy of consumption and customer success plans with the Customer Success Account Manager, and drive next best actions that generate incremental Cloud pipeline.
Guide workload security, privacy, governance, sovereignty, reliability, performance, capacity, and cost optimization, including service and model retirements, and apply responsible AI principles to production AI and agent scenarios.
Resolve technical blockers with account teams, partners, and engineering; act as the Voice of the Customer by sharing adoption issues, capacity constraints, product gaps, and platform readiness feedback.
Create and reuse solution accelerators, reference architectures, and repeatable IP that help customers deploy faster, and support customer and partner skilling through technical workshops and readiness activities across data platforms, AI apps, agents, and GitHub.
Continuously build expertise in Azure AI Foundry, Copilot Studio, Agent365, GitHub and GitHub Copilot, Microsoft Fabric, Azure Databricks, Microsoft Purview, Azure databases, app platforms, containers, integration services, and DevOps; demonstrate a growth mindset by sharing knowledge and customer success stories, mentoring others, and contributing to internal and external technical communities.
Other Embody our culture and values
Qualifications
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business, or related field AND 4+ years experience in Cloud & AI platform technologies, including Azure architecture, AI and agents, GitHub, Agentic DevOps, AI Agent development, data platforms, application modernization, resiliency, security, and production-scale cloud delivery, information technology (IT) consulting/support, systems administration, network operations, software development/support, technology solutions, practice development, architecture, and/or consulting
OR equivalent experience
Other Requirements
​This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Candidates must have authorization to work in the United States that does not now or in the future require employer sponsorship.​
Preferred Qualification s
5+ years of technical enterprise experience in one or more of the following Cloud & AI technology areas: Data platforms and analytics: Microsoft Fabric, Azure Databricks, Azure databases (SQL, Cosmos DB, PostgreSQL), data engineering, or Microsoft Purview governance
AI applications and agents: Azure AI Foundry, Copilot Studio, agent frameworks, LLM/RAG application development, or responsible AI
Application platforms and developer tooling: GitHub, GitHub Copilot, containers (AKS), serverless, integration services, or DevOps/Agentic DevOps
5+ years of experience designing and delivering secure, scalable data and AI solutions, from architecture and proof of concept through production deployment, with a focus on measurable business value and customer adoption.
3+ years of experience owning end-to-end technical delivery results, including resolving complex blockers and addressing security, privacy, governance, reliability, performance, cost optimization, and responsible AI considerations.
5+ years experience across cloud, data, AI, application, and developer platforms, with a growth mindset demonstrated through reusable solution development, technical skilling, knowledge sharing, mentoring, and engagement with technical communities

Azure AI Engineer Associate (AI-102)

title: Senior Consulting Project Manager - CTJ - TS/SCI
description:
Overview
Engages with customer stakeholders to develop partnerships, leveraging broad technical expertise. Drives customer satisfaction by engaging with customers stakeholders in a positive manner, reviewing and analyzing customer feedback, and leveraging trusted relationships with key internal resources to act as the voice of the customer. Adheres to project compliance standards and requirements of the contract and accommodates customer compliance standards. Drives project initiation for projects of medium complexity by delivering a workstream within a larger project/program. Facilitates contracting process for partner resources by briefing partners, coordinating partner candidate interviews, and identifying and acclimating partner resources to the team. Develops detailed project management plan to drive predictable delivery for projects of medium complexity or supports senior colleagues in projects of high complexity. Provides review of defined metrics, proactively monitors and tracks risks, ensures timely completion and quality of deliverables, and manages stakeholder communications. Drives timely project closure by ensuring completion of project sign off tasks. Applies advanced knowledge across project management principle areas, contributes at local team-wide level to share knowledge and support others, serves as a mentor to colleagues to grow identified skill gaps, and participates in cross-border mentoring and peer alignment to share lessons learned on challenging projects.
Responsibilities
Account Delivery Management
Contributes to consumption activities, through others (e.g., Customer Success resources), for customers by identifying blockers to consumption goals and enabling customers, through internal teams, to get the full value of their purchases. Holds accountability for project delivery forecast.
Drives and maintains obligations to customer across the delivery lifecycle including envisioning, solution development, delivery planning, cloud consumption and usage, delivery management while ensuring adherence to security best practices in partnership with Solution Area SMEs. Ensures that customer-required or market-required security certifications are active. Leads or participates in steering committee meetings with strategic customers to discuss progress toward delivery success.
Supports relationships with key stakeholders in the customer portfolio to ensure service delivery is on track and issues are being anticipated, identified, and managed. Communicates current view of delivery to customer stakeholders, as appropriate.
Collaborates with Sales to support contract setup, signature, compliance, and execution from deal approvals to invoicing and closure. Manages areas of fiscal responsibility within project portfolio, staying within budget while driving engagement profitability and risk management.
Business Growth
Looks for or creates opportunities to maximize timely cloud consumption through current deliveries. Identifies new opportunities with customers and facilitates follow up conversations with customers on Consumption both strategically and operational, and to accelerate delivery or prevent delivery delays.
Demonstrates accountability for the financial health of a project or program (e.g., revenue attainment, accurate forecasting, cost management, and utilization, skills, and capacity planning). Identifies opportunities to accelerate and drive consumption and delivery. Owns and drives backlog risk management. Drives incremental business on top of existing projects and programs through next step proposals, conducts customer discussions related to next stage proposal (NSP) and other opportunities. Engages in the pursuit cycle to ensure deals are structured appropriately. Supports and contributes to rhythm of business (ROB) and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) forecasting.
Closure
Drives timely project closure by ensuring completion of project sign off tasks (e.g., system closeout updates, deletion of customer data, Deliverable Acceptance Form). Drives incremental process improvement by reflecting on and sharing lessons learned across teams, creating and suggesting improvements to intellectual property (IP), providing feedback to managers on team member performance, and conducting closeout interviews with team members.
Applies advanced knowledge across project management principle areas to execution and delivery, contributes at local team-wide level to share knowledge and support others, serves as a mentor to less experienced colleagues to grow identified skill gaps, and participates in cross-border mentoring and peer alignment to share lessons learned on challenging projects.
Contracting
Facilitates contracting process for customer and partner resources (e.g., contractors, vendors) by briefing partners, coordinating partner candidate interviews, and identifying and acclimating partner resources to the team. Supports negotiation and structuring of fixed-fee subcontractor contracts with oversight from senior colleagues. Monitors and initiates Amendments, Delivery Acceptance, Proof of Delivery, and Invoicing processes. Reviews contracts according to security and data governance standards. Provides session on SFI/SBD to the onboarding partner team
Initiation
Drives project initiation for projects of medium complexity (e.g., multiple offerings, and/or supports projects of high complexity (e.g., tailored offerings, high visibility, high impact, market making) by delivering a workstream within a larger project/program, by driving commitment of delivery resources, assigning resources, assisting in sourcing and qualifying partner resources, and creating work breakdown structures (WBSs) with delivery team. Drives checklist and process finalization for Secure Future Initiative (SFI) with team and customers
Balances needs across projects in challenging situations (e.g., scarce technical resources), with support from senior colleagues as needed, and collaborates with other groups (e.g., resource managers, Global Delivery Center) on integrated planning and organization of onshore/offshore projects.
Intellectual Property (IP)
Researches and proactively shares intellectual property (IP) and provides recommendations for improvement including submitting new IP. Holds others accountable for reusing appropriate IP and collective knowledge by enforcing use of processes and artifacts with team members.
Monitoring and Controlling
Ensures timely completion and quality of deliverables (e.g., documents) and tracking of agreed upon metrics for projects of standard complexity by applying quality management techniques (e.g., benchmarking, interviews) for collecting data. Uses analyses to identify solutions to systemic issues.
Manages finances for projects with mid-size to large scopes and budgets by balancing funding and resources across workstreams, performing analyses, and leveraging cost management experience and expertise. Aims to reduce cost and improve delivery margin without impact to quality or customer experience and understands impact of decisions on the broader business (e.g., profits and losses [P&L], accrual-based accounting).
Discusses and confirms Microsoft change control processes at kickoff with customer. Anticipates changes and proactively addresses by probing to ensure change can happen smoothly early in the process. Tests process before initiating formal change.
Orchestrates and oversees a broad range of project metrics on midsize to large projects with high visibility (e.g., Vice President-level). Proactively ensures adherence to key performance indicators (KPIs) and provides strategic direction to drive success throughout project lifecycle.
Proactively manages risks (including security risks) and issues within projects of standard complexity, leveraging technical knowledge and previous experience to evaluate risks, perform qualitative analyses (e.g., probability, impact, urgency), create risk management plans, establish processes, and work with cross-functional groups and leaders to mitigate identified risks. Contributes to recovery efforts and ensures tools are updated. Manages issue closure as a high priority. Ensures that the mandatory Information Security Risk Assessment (ISRA) is completed during project initiation, is regularly reviewed, and is signed off by accredited InfoSec Delivery Compliance Leads during delivery. Reports Security and Data Compliance breaches in a timely manner (using ReportItNow and other pertinent customer reporting outlets as applicable), informing both internal and external stakeholders.
Manages stakeholder communications on project health, issues, and financial performance for mid-size to large deals throughout entire project lifecycle, tailoring communications to the audience. Tracks and maintains customer deliverables.
Planning
Develops detailed project management plan to drive predictable delivery for projects of medium complexity or supports senior colleagues in projects of high complexity, leveraging existing materials and experience to drive scope, resources, and Microsoft project schedule in alignment and collaboration with customer plan. Ensures use of baselining, resource load balancing, and application of work effort, dependency management, contingency planning, and utilization of software (e.g., Timeline).
Establishes clear expectations and accountabilities (e.g., reconfirm scope, Responsible-Accountable-Consulted-Informed matrix) with all project team members (e.g., consultants) and stakeholders for teams of medium complexity by leading internal and external kick-off meetings (e.g., sales to delivery handoff, formal kick-off meetings). Integrates security-first mindset into expectations for self and others. Proactively engages broad set of internal and external stakeholders, including those who are impacted by project scope/outcome, but not directly involved (e.g., Enterprise Operating Unit, India Global Delivery, customer stakeholders) and engages subject matter experts in holistic planning activities, including team validation.
Presales
Contributes to pre-sales for medium-impact projects by articulating the business value proposition associated with the project/change and considering associated complexities and risks to ensure feasibility of commercial offer. Participates in review of proposed scope and assists in developing Statement of Work (SOW), Work Breakdown Structures (WBSs), estimates, preliminary risk assessments, etc. Ensures that ISD consulting deal appropriately includes Delivery Compliance, Privacy & Security (DCPS) package to fund Secure?by?Default activities.
Relationship Development
Drives customer satisfaction by engaging with customers stakeholders in a positive manner, reviewing and analyzing customer feedback, and leveraging trusted relationships with key internal resources to act as the voice of the customer. Manages expectations with political sensitivity by leading Success Expectation discussions with customer, and documenting, executing, and monitoring through customer and partner experience (CPE).
Engages with customer stakeholders to develop partnerships, leveraging broad technical expertise. Manages escalations or ensures resolution of escalations with customer stakeholders through tailored corrective action (e.g., education) and overcomes ambiguous situations as needed. Learns to leverage project sponsors and internal network to influence stakeholders and resolve situations.
Adheres to project compliance standards (e.g., confidentiality, privacy, security) and requirements of the contract and accommodates customer compliance standards, including managing compliance-related complexities (e.g., high sensitivity to confidentiality). Champions compliance by contributing to knowledge sharing across teams to build compliance capability of others.
Qualifications
Required/minimum qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in related field AND 2+ years experience in project management OR equivalent experience.
Other Requirements
The successful candidate must have an active U.S. Government Top Secret/SCI Security Clearance .   Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. Failure to maintain or obtain the appropriate clearance and/or customer screening requirements may result in employment action up to and including termination.
Clearance Verification: This position requires successful verification of the stated security clearance to meet federal government customer requirements. You will be asked to provide clearance verification information prior to an offer of employment.
Citizenship & Citizenship Verification: This position requires verification of U.S citizenship due to citizenship-based legal restrictions. Specifically, this position supports United States federal, state, and/or local United States government agency customers and is subject to certain citizenship-based restrictions where required or permitted by applicable law. To meet this legal requirement, citizenship will be verified via a valid passport.
Citizenship & Citizenship Verification:  This role will require access to information that is controlled for export under U.S. export control regulations, potentially under the International Traffic in Arms Regulations or the Export Administration Regulations.  As a condition of employment, the successful candidate will be required to provide proof of citizenship, for assessment of eligibility to access the export-controlled information.  To meet this legal requirement, citizenship will be verified via a valid passport.
Preferred/Additional Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in related field AND 8+ years experience in project management OR equivalent experience.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
4+ years financial management experience.
Agile certification, Scrum Master, Agile Certified Practitioner (PMI-ACP), or Professional Scrum Master One (PSM1) certification.

title: Senior Creative Technologist
location: United States, California, Mountain View; United States, Washington, Seattle; United States, New York, New York
description:
Overview
We are looking for a multidisciplinary AIX Creative Technologist who blends the instincts of a designer, the creative vision of a storyteller, and the technical fluency of a creative engineer. Embedded within the Creative Studio, you will help imagine and shape the future of Copilot and AI experiences by exploring new product ideas, features, interactions, and embodied AI characters, while building working prototypes that bring those possibilities to life.
This role brings together product design, interaction design, animation, AI, storytelling, and software development. You will explore emerging technologies, experiment with new forms of human–AI interaction, and develop prototypes, tools, and reusable systems that help move ideas from early exploration toward real product experiences.
The ideal candidate is as comfortable imagining new product possibilities and crafting intuitive, expressive experiences as writing code, connecting systems, and debugging prototypes. You should bring deep expertise in at least one discipline and a demonstrated ability to bridge creative thinking and technical execution.
The future of Copilot and AI must be experienced, not just imagined. From entirely new product ideas, features, and interactions to embodied AI characters and how they move, speak, behave, and respond, the most compelling possibilities come to life through tangible, interactive experiences that people can see, feel, and explore.
You will help build the Creative Studio’s ability to imagine, prototype, validate, and bring these ideas to life—connecting creative strategy, design, storytelling, and emerging technologies to new product possibilities, strengthening shared technical capabilities, and bridging the gap between creative vision and implementation.
Responsibilities
Develop and prototype future AI experiences. Translate blue-sky Copilot and AI product ideas, narratives, and creative concepts into compelling UI explorations, UX flows, interactive demos, and working prototypes that advance the product experience, brand, identity, and creative vision.
Design embodied AI characters and experiences. Shape character identity, visual language, motion, expression, personality, and behavior across products and platforms, including onboarding, customization, voice, and feedback systems that make AI experiences intuitive, expressive, and trustworthy.
Build interactive, real-time systems. Develop, debug, and optimize character animation, input, and response systems, connecting UI frameworks such as React, real-time rendering technologies such as Babylon.js, and AI services into cohesive, performant experiences across platforms, including mobile.
Prototype with AI agents and emerging technologies. Experiment with conversational, multimodal, generative, and multi-agent systems, integrating models, tools, and services to coordinate actions, manage state, and explore new ways people interact with AI.
Bridge creative vision and engineering execution. Build everything from lightweight experiments to production-minded prototypes, working within established code architectures and engineering frameworks to develop maintainable, reusable components and evaluate technical feasibility.
Collaborate, validate, and scale ideas. Partner with Research, Design, Product, and Engineering to test tension, trust, and emotional response, refine concepts, and develop shared tools, workflows, and design patterns that accelerate creative exploration and implementation across the studio.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
Master's Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Graphic Design, Product Design, Visual Design, Human Computer Interaction, or related field AND 3+ years experience working in product or service design and/or shipping production code
OR Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Graphic Design, Product Design, Visual Design, Human Computer Interaction, or related field AND 4+ years experience working in product or service design and/or shipping production code
OR equivalent experience.
Preferred Qualifications:
Creative Design & Prototyping
A portfolio demonstrating compelling interactive experiences and your specific contributions to design and implementation, including vision demos, UI/UX explorations, and functional product prototypes.
Strong creative judgment in interaction design, animation, motion, character behavior, visual storytelling, or related disciplines.
The ability to translate broad strategic ideas into focused, tangible prototypes, balancing creative ambition with feasibility, quality, and speed.
Technical Development & Real-Time Systems
Hands-on programming experience with the ability to independently build, integrate, troubleshoot, and iterate on interactive prototypes.
Proficiency in JavaScript and WebGL, with experience connecting web UI and real-time 3D using React, Babylon.js, or comparable technologies.
Experience with real-time development environments such as Unity, Unreal Engine, web-based 3D, or similar technology stacks.
Understanding software architecture, existing codebases, and engineering practices, including finite state machines (FSMs), state synchronization, event handling, and lifecycle management.
Experience optimizing performance across platforms, particularly mobile, balancing visual quality, rendering cost, memory, loading times, and responsiveness.
AI & Emerging Technologies
Hands-on experience working with AI agents, including integrating models, tools, and services into interactive, user-facing experiences.
A track record of developing or shipping experiences using emerging technologies such as real-time 3D, games, generative AI, VR, or AR.
Product & Human-Centered Experience Design
An understanding of human-centered design and how timing, feedback, personality, and behavior influence clarity, usability, and trust.
Experience developing enterprise or consumer software products, with an appreciation for accessibility, reliability, maintainability, and long-term usability beyond one-off demos or entertainment experiences.
Collaboration & Communication
Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work across Creative, Research, Product, and Engineering to develop, evaluate, and advance ideas from early exploration toward implementation.

title: Senior Critical Environment Technician (Night Shift)
description:
Overview
As a Senior Critical Environment Technician (CET) in Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) team, you will maintain the critical infrastructure that keeps our Datacenters up and running. This could be anything from coordinating with supplier/vendors, working closely with Management to address operational, risk and safety situations, mentoring other CE Technicians, having a hands-on understanding on how critical environment equipment works, performing various types of maintenance, responding to onsite incidents while coordinating with other critical facilities professionals, and using telemetry and other platforms to monitor equipment performance and operations.
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Critical Environment Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties.
Responsibilities
Critical Environment Culture
May travel up to 25%, typically domestically for training and/or supporting another site. May work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.
Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance
Provides necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site based on the appropriate procedure levels of risk (LOR). Takes part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Recognizes circumstances when to stop supplier/vendor work to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates per appropriate LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Reviews and completes appropriate work orders to support approval of vendor supplier field service reports or invoices.
Performs troubleshooting of equipment and systems independently within their trained discipline(s). Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Communicates and/or escalates troubleshooting issues or anomalies with assistance from more experienced colleagues. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment works within disciplines they have been trained.
Performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs (e.g., basic replacements, changing of parts) for specific disciplines and equipment for which they have been trained, following methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) with minimal supervision - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Performs lower level maintenance with minimal supervision, and may resolve high level issues with support from more experienced colleagues. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Maintains all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance.
Prepares and submits required reports (e.g., turnover, preventative maintenance [PM]) as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates. Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for appropriately leveled procedures to ensure safe and reliable execution. Documents completed work using approved tools and procedural templates for more experienced technician review. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments.
Develops an understanding of method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Coordinates activities and associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities.
Equipment and Systems Operations
Works on tasks (e.g., making rounds, initial assessments on equipment performance) as assigned with varying levels of supervision, sometimes minimal. Supports senior colleagues as an assistant. Builds knowledge in operating equipment and systems within a set discipline (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls). Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
Performs monitoring physical inspection of critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds for unsafe or abnormal conditions. Understands critical system alarms for single discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) within the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify critical alarms. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems.
Safely responds to and stabilizes abnormal conditions within the required timeframes for various abnormal facility events within data center with minimal supervision, utilizing emergency operating procedures (EOPs). Gathers necessary information and participates in the creation of incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur. Customer Service
Maintains a strong focus to understand the impact of their work when completing tickets and assigned Inventory and Asset Management (IAM) tasks. Communicates across Data Center teams (e.g., Site Services, Critical Environment, Facility Management, Security, Vendors, Safety, Supply Chain), and supports Microsoft and non-Microsoft gear deliveries. Ensures IAM tasks are completed accurately as requested, as well as meet company and industry standards and policies. Builds strong working relationships with customers. Identifies, coordinates, manages expectations, and offers alternatives when defining stakeholder solutions in light of ongoing company standards, operations, and procedures (e.g., schedule, technical feasibility, policy, procedure, tools).
Data Bearing Device (DBD) Destruction

Coordinates with and oversees any third-party vendors who perform DBD destruction as necessary. Begins to act as a resource for the decommissioning process to ensure customer security is maintained, performing data bearing devices (DBD) destruction as necessary. Inbound and Outbound Logistics

Documents inbound/outbound packages. Receives, confirms, tracks, stores, dispatches, and delivers material from the warehouse to destinations, including production facilities, retail stores, and corporate offices. Procurement

description:
About the Team

The Product Policy team develops and implements policies that shape how OpenAI’s technology is built and used. We work with teams across the company to turn complex questions about AI’s benefits and risks into practical guidance for responsible research, product development, and deployment.

About the Role

We are hiring a senior applied scientist to study how AI affects people and society using OpenAI production data, experiments, and social science methods. This role sits at the intersection of applied social science, AI, and product policy. The scientist will own research from an ambiguous question through study design, data collection and analysis, methodological validation, and recommendations. Their work will inform product and policy decisions and, where appropriate, contribute to external publications. We are looking for a hands-on empirical social scientist with exceptional methodological judgment.

In this role, you will:

 - Develop and execute a research agenda on AI’s social impact, including effects on well-being, learning, social connection, trust, and human decision-making, in partnership with product and policy teams.

 - Own empirical studies end to end: define the question and estimand, choose the design, build the dataset, conduct the analysis, and explain what the evidence supports.

 - Develop and validate measures of social outcomes, including human and LLM-assisted annotations; assess measurement error, subgroup performance, and drift.

 - Partner with Product Policy, Research, Product, Data Science, Engineering, UXR, Legal, and domain experts; contribute rigorous work to external publications when appropriate.

 - A PhD or equivalent research experience in sociology, political science, psychology, communication, computational social science, or a related empirical field, with demonstrated independent research ownership.

 - Strong SQL and Python or R skills, with experience independently constructing and analyzing complex behavioral datasets and producing reproducible research.

 - A record of research that informs consequential decisions about technology and people, with the judgment to identify both useful findings and unresolved uncertainty.

description:
About the Team

Customer Education helps customers build the practical skills and confidence to use AI and OpenAI products safely and effectively. We bring together customer insight, learning and enablement expertise, product signals, and measurement to help organizations move from access to durable adoption.

Within Customer Education, the Certification team helps individuals demonstrate competence for in-demand AI skills and helps customers and partners validate that their workforce has the skills they need to meet their AI-enabled business goals. Our work centers on the belief that learners should understand where to go to build skills and capabilities, how to demonstrate them, and what to pursue next. Similarly, Enterprise leaders should understand what each credential signifies and how it supports workforce readiness. We do this with transparency for the overall OpenAI credential framework and providing trusted, role-based certifications that verify practical capability.

About the Role

As Certification Architect, you will define the framework, standards, and assessment architecture that make OpenAI certifications a trusted signal of demonstrated capability.

This is a senior hands-on role on the Certification team that will build reusable foundations for a growing portfolio: clear competency standards, defensible assessments, scalable in-product delivery, and evidence of continued competence.

We’re looking for someone who combines deep certification and assessment expertise with the ability to innovate new and meaningful ways to demonstrate practical AI competence. You will work closely with certification specialists, technical subject matter experts, learning product and engineering teams, operations and policy partners, and stakeholders across the go-to-market organization.

The program is early, and you will help shape how people demonstrate capability in ChatGPT and Codex. Success means building standards that are rigorous, usable, and adaptable as AI technology and professional roles evolve.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Own the credential framework and shared competency standards, distinguishing completed learning, demonstrated skills, and formal certification, with clear capability claims and evidence requirements for each.

 - Establish reusable assessment standards and guidance for certification pods across job-task analysis, competency models, assessment blueprints, performance tasks, scoring rubrics, and passing standards.

 - Own the validation approach and evidence documentation requirements. Partner with pod leaders to validate certification proposals against job relevance, representative task coverage, scoring consistency, fairness, and appropriate interpretation of results.

 - Define exam delivery architecture and requirements with product, engineering, operations, and third parties, spanning registration, identity verification, monitoring, permitted assistance, evidence capture, scoring, human review, appeals, customer support, and record management.

 - Define expectations for continued competence validation post-assessment.

 - Partner with learning, operations, policy, legal, privacy, security, and accessibility teams to align preparation with competencies while protecting assessment integrity and establishing appropriate evidence access, retention, accommodations, and review processes.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have 10+ years experience designing and delivering professional technical IT industry certifications or assessments that support credible claims about what people can do.

 - Have led design of performance-based assessments for AI, software development, technical architecture, or customer-facing implementation roles.

 - Have built credential frameworks, competency models, or shared assessment standards that work across multiple roles or programs.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a senior individual contributor to support revenue growth across the Americas (AMER) by helping sales teams structure and close commercially sound deals. You will balance speed and responsiveness with pricing discipline, consistent processes, and appropriate financial and commercial controls.

In this role, you will be the day-to-day Deal Operations partner for AMER account teams, reviewing pricing, discounts, and commercial terms across new business, renewals, and expansions. You will guide sellers through deal requirements, evaluate non-standard requests, and coordinate the approvals needed to move opportunities through contracting and closure.

You will also develop scalable workflows, guidance, and tools that improve deal turnaround times, documentation quality, and consistency across the region.

This role partners closely with Sales, Finance, Legal, Pricing, and Revenue Operations, with Product and other teams engaged as needed, to resolve deal issues and support accurate execution from quote through contract and booking.

In this role, you will:

 - Serve as the primary Deal Operations contact for AMER account teams, managing deal intake, prioritizing requests, and guiding sellers through pricing, review, and approval processes.

 - Review quotes and proposed commercial terms, including discounts, payment schedules, contract duration, and customer commitments, for accuracy and alignment with pricing guidelines and commercial policies.

 - Strong financial modeling and analytical skills, including experience assessing pricing, discounts, revenue, margins, and deal profitability.

 - Knowledge of enterprise software commercial terms and subscription or consumption-based business models, with the judgment to identify issues that require Legal or Finance review.

 - Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to explain commercial tradeoffs, make clear recommendations, and coordinate timely decisions across teams.

 - Experience with CRM systems, configure-price-quote (CPQ) tools, and contract management platforms, along with strong spreadsheet skills.

 - Attention to detail and a track record of improving approval workflows, documentation, and operational processes as a business scales.

 - Sound commercial judgment and the ability to manage competing priorities and tight deadlines while maintaining accuracy and appropriate controls.

 - A collaborative, hands-on approach to supporting sales teams and familiarity with using AI and automation to improve deal workflows and productivity.

description:
About the Team

The Frontier Robustness team advances the science of securing frontier AI systems. We develop new methods to keep increasingly capable models contained, observable, and under human control, focusing on the sandboxes, shared research infrastructure, and protective systems used during model development and evaluation.

We use our most capable models to discover and combine weaknesses across the security stack, studying how they might escape containment, communicate through unauthorized channels, or evade monitoring. We turn these findings into new defenses and test whether protections hold as models, environments, and attack strategies change.



About the Role

We are looking for a researcher to develop and test new methods for securing frontier AI systems. You will investigate open-ended questions about model behavior, containment, and safeguards—designing experiments, building evaluations, and developing defenses where established approaches may be insufficient. You will work closely with the Security organization to define the problems and translate research findings into practical protections.

You will take research from an initial question and threat model through experiment design, reproducible findings, and tested defenses. You will write code, build tools and prototypes, and work closely with researchers and infrastructure owners to turn new ideas into safeguards that work in practice. This requires sound security judgment, comfort with uncertainty, and the ability to devise solutions to problems without established answers. This role is based in San Francisco.



In this role, you will:

 - Design and run experiments using frontier models and hands-on security techniques to discover failure modes in sandboxes, research infrastructure, and the services models can reach. Reproduce vulnerabilities and assess their impact.

 - Develop threat models and novel adversarial tests for attacks that cross multiple security boundaries, including sandbox escapes, unauthorized communication between agents, and access to sensitive data or systems through shared services.

 - Invent, prototype, and evaluate defenses that strengthen isolation and limit the impact of a compromised boundary. Study agent permissions and tool configurations to identify excessive access and build layered protections with infrastructure owners.

 - Develop and red-team model-based safeguards and monitors of model reasoning and actions. Investigate evasion, test new monitoring techniques, and measure when protections detect or prevent unsafe behavior.

 - Develop automated adversarial tests and repeatable evaluations to measure progress as model capabilities, configurations, and attack strategies change. Assess whether defenses generalize to new attacks, verify fixes, and identify regressions.

 - Partner across Research, Security, and infrastructure teams, including Agent Security, to prioritize risks and turn findings into deployed improvements while accounting for performance and researcher workflows.
   
   

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have hands-on experience conducting research with large language models, including designing and running experiments and evaluating model behavior.

 - Can turn an open-ended question into a clear hypothesis, build reproducible experiments at scale, and use the results to develop or improve a method.

 - Can design rigorous evaluations, investigate unexpected results, and test whether findings hold across different models, environments, and attack strategies.

 - Write and debug code independently, build research tools and prototypes, and carry ideas through experimentation.

 - Bring practical security experience relevant to this work, such as sandboxing, vulnerability research, adversarial testing, or detection and monitoring.

description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE ROLE
Director of Facilities
The Director of Facilities will have end-to-end accountability for the operational performance, physical condition, safety, functionality, and employee experience of Quince's headquarters in both San Francisco and Palo Alto.  This is a hands-on role that will require on-location presence in both locations weekly.
A defining responsibility of this position will be helping Quince transition into a significantly larger, more complex headquarters building in San Francisco. The Director will partner with internal leadership, the relocation project manager, architects, contractors, and service providers to ensure the new headquarters is fully operational, exceptionally maintained, and equipped to support the company's continued growth.  The role will
Following the relocation, this leader will oversee all aspects of headquarters facilities operations, including building systems, maintenance, workplace services, security coordination, vendor management, budgets, sample and fabric library operations, and ongoing improvements.
The Director will also lead a team of Sample and Fabric Library Coordinators, ensuring product samples and fabric materials are accurately tracked, organized, maintained, and readily accessible to Quince's merchandising, product development, design, and other internal teams.
Responsibilities
1. New Headquarters Relocation & Operational Readiness
Play a central leadership role in Quince's relocation to a substantially larger and more comprehensive headquarters in San Francisco.
Partner with the relocation project manager, architects, construction teams, designers, IT, Security, and executive leadership to ensure a successful transition.
Develop and execute a comprehensive facilities operational-readiness plan for the new headquarters.
Oversee building systems commissioning, operational testing, inspections, and facilities handover.
Establish required maintenance programs, vendor contracts, workplace services, and operating procedures prior to occupancy.
Ensure the new headquarters supports a significantly larger employee population and more complex workplace services.
Coordinate the readiness of conference facilities, employee amenities, shared spaces, and sample and fabric library areas.
Develop staffing plans, operating budgets, and service standards appropriate for the new facility.

We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.

Success in this role means consistently delivering 98%+ on-time delivery, maintaining first-pass yield of ≥98%, achieving zero customer returns attributable to manufacturing defects, building a real-time order tracking system that provides complete visibility from factory to end customer, and enabling Quince to scale jewelry MTO volume while maintaining the highest quality standards. Own end-to-end production planning and scheduling across manufacturing partners; translate demand forecasts into detailed daily/weekly production workflows that meet the 3-week delivery window.

Establish and maintain quality control standards across manufacturing partners; monitor defect rates, first-pass yield, escalate quality misses immediately.
Serve as primary operational liaison with manufacturing partners and conduct weekly operational reviews covering schedule adherence, quality, delivery performance, capacity, and risk mitigation with domestic and international suppliers.
Coordinate logistics and fulfillment; ensure correct packaging, labeling, and shipment to freight forwarders; track deliveries through final customer receipt and manage any post-delivery issues.
Create daily MTO standup and weekly operational dashboard tracking on-time delivery, defect rates, lead times, inventory levels, and production bottlenecks; provide monthly reporting to leadership.
Monitor and respond to production risks in real-time; flag orders at risk of missing the 3-week window within 24 hours; drive rapid problem-solving across manufacturing, quality, and logistics.
Qualifications
Required:
Minimum 5 years of jewelry manufacturing experience, including direct exposure to Jewelry manufacturing, quality control, and production management processes.
Proven track record of managing production workflows, schedules, and timelines in jewelry or related manufacturing environments, with experience delivering on accelerated timelines.
Direct experience tracking orders and managing fulfillment from factory through shipping and customer delivery (end-to-end visibility and accountability).
Demonstrated ability to manage quality control, defect tracking, root-cause analysis, and corrective action closure in a production environment.
Strong experience coordinating with manufacturing partners or managing supplier relationships in production-critical roles; comfort with cross-partner communication and escalation.
Strong Excel/Google Sheets skills and experience building or managing production tracking systems (ERP, MES, custom dashboards); ability to learn new software tools quickly.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; comfort with data-driven decisions and identifying process improvements from operational metrics.
Exceptional written and verbal communication; ability to create clear, actionable reports and escalation summaries for multiple stakeholders.
Obsessive attention to detail; defects and missed deadlines are intolerable to you; you catch problems before they reach customers.
Calm under pressure; ability to manage competing priorities and operational escalations with composure and rapid decision-making.
Collaborative and relationship-oriented; you build strong partnerships with manufacturing teams, quality leads, logistics partners, and cross-functional stakeholders.
Experience working cross-functionally with merchandising, sourcing, and production teams

description:
As an S&C Electric team member, you’ll work on projects that have real-world impact. You’ll help transform the grid for resilient and reliable power worldwide. S&C has more than a 100-year history of innovation and has been 100% employee-owned since 2012. We continue this legacy as a trusted, forward-thinking leader in the electrical industry. You will advance a safer, more reliable, and more resilient electrical grid. Our products help the grid adapt to severe weather and transition to clean energy. We’re big enough to be a respected industry leader but small enough for you to impact our company directly. Our commitment gives you opportunities to impact on and off the job positively. Join S&C to make an impact on tomorrow’s energy challenges and become an employee-owner.
Hours
7:30 am – 4:00 pm On-Site (Chicago, IL)
At S&C, we are dedicated to providing competitive and equitable compensation for all our team members, and we are committed to transparency in our pay practices. The estimated annual base salary range for this position is $69,740 - $91,309.00. Individual pay within this salary range is determined by several compensable factors, including performance, knowledge, job-related skills and experience, and relevant education or training. This role is also eligible for S&C’s annual incentive plan (AIP), subject to eligibility criteria.
Join Our Team as a Material Planner!
S&C Electric Company is seeking a dynamic individual to join our Lateral Automation Value Stream. As a Material Planner, you’ll be crucial in ensuring smooth operations and supporting our diverse team. The Material Planner plays a critical role within the value stream organization, responsible for ensuring uninterrupted material availability to support production while optimizing inventory levels. The Material Planner is accountable for clear-to-build (CTB) management, balancing demand and supply, and maintaining optimal stocking strategies. This position serves as a key problem solver within Oracle ERP and provides material readiness guidance to scheduling teams to support on-time production execution.
Key Responsibilities:
Material Planning & Clear-to-Build Management
Maintain Clear-to-Build (CTB) status to ensure production readiness across the value stream.
Proactively identify material constraints and partner with other members of the team to drive resolution to prevent production disruptions.
Align material availability with production schedules and customer demand.
Demand & Supply Balancing
Analyze demand signals and translate them into accurate material requirements.
Balance supply and demand through effective planning, prioritization, and scenario analysis.
Adjust plans in response to demand changes, supply disruptions, or inventory imbalances.
Inventory Management
Establish and manage safety stock and stocking levels to ensure optimal inventory investment while minimizing risk.
Segment inventory via ABC/XYZ analysis.
Monitor inventory health (excess, obsolete, and slow-moving materials) and drive corrective actions.
Partner with assembly to implement cycle count program.
Coordinate with Procurement and suppliers to manage inventory strategies, improve material flow, and ensure components are delivered to the point of use in support of production schedules.
Manage inventory locator creation and maintenance, ensuring accurate material tracking and proper movement of inventory into, within, and out of designated storage locations.
Analyze and disposition existing inventory impacted by engineering changes to minimize obsolescence and excess costs.
ERP & System Management
Utilize Oracle ERP for material planning, purchase requisitions, inventory tracking, and data accuracy.
Troubleshoot and resolve planning and system-related issues within Oracle.
Ensure accurate master data (planning factors, ordering methods, and locator integrity) to support effective planning.
Support purchase order management, expedite critical materials, and mitigate shortages.
Problem Solving & Continuous Improvement
Initiate root cause analysis and corrective actions for material shortages and supply interruptions.
Make recommendations that drive continuous improvement in planning processes, inventory accuracy, and system utilization.
Implement best practices such as JIT, Kanban, and lean material flow concepts where applicable.
What you’ll need to succeed:
Required
Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, or related field required
2-3+ years of experience in material planning, supply chain, purchasing, or manufacturing operations
ASCM/APICS Certification (CPIM, CSCP, or CTSC) preferred
Experience in ERP systems (Oracle preferred; SAP or similar acceptable)
Strong proficiency in ERP systems (Oracle, SAP, or equivalent)
Advanced Excel skills (data analysis, forecasting, modeling)
Understanding of MRP, inventory control, and supply chain processes
Analytical Thinking: Ability to analyze complex data and make informed decisions
Problem-Solving: Strong capability to resolve material and system issues quickly
Attention to Detail: High level of accuracy in planning and system data
Communication & Collaboration: Effective cross-functional and supplier communication
Adaptability: Ability to manage shifting priorities in a dynamic production environment
Execution Focus: Bias toward action and results in critical supply situations
